title: 3 x Chocolate Hazelnut Snack Bar Bundle - 100% Raw Whole Foods
Adobo Black Bean Tostadas With Shredded Lettuce, Lime Cashew Crema, Avocado & Salsa Macha

steps.raw_text: Take out a saucepan and preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare saucepan
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C or 180°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Traditionally tostadas are shallow fried in oil for 30 seconds on each side, which you can do if you want them to turn really crispy. However for our healthier, oil-free version, simply pop the tacos onto a baking tray with space in between them and bake for 8 minutes or until crispy, flipping half way.
steps.label: Bake tacos on baking tray
steps.notes: Bake for 8 minutes, flipping halfway, or until crispy. Alternatively, shallow fry in oil for 30 seconds per side.

steps.raw_text: Drain the black beans and empty into your saucepan along with the smoky adobo sauce , place over a medium heat and warm through, stirring occasionally, until piping hot, around 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if it starts to stick at the bottom. Roughly mash around half of the beans with a fork and set aside.
steps.label: Warm and mash black beans
steps.notes: Warm over medium heat for around 5 minutes until piping hot. Add water if sticking. Mash half with a fork.

steps.raw_text: Finely shred the baby gem by cutting horizontally across the head. De-stone the avocado and cut into thin slices flat side down. If you're feeling fancy you could fan the avocado for a more elevated final presentation. Using the palm of your hand, carefully push the avocado down and away from yourself to open it up like a fan without the slices breaking. Cut the lime into wedges.
steps.label: Shred lettuce and slice avocado
steps.notes: Finely shred baby gem lettuce, slice and optionally fan the avocado, and cut the lime into wedges.

steps.raw_text: Lay everything out on your table and then start building your tostadas. Start with a layer of black beans , then shredded lettuce , dress the lettuce with a drizzle of cashew crema , top with some slices of avocado and a final drizzle of salsa macha . Finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice, and enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve the tostadas
steps.notes: Layer beans, lettuce, cashew crema, avocado, salsa macha, and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Afghan Aubergine (Borani Banjan) With Saucy Spiced Lentils, Garlic Yoghurt, Fresh Mint & Pillowy Flatbreads

steps.raw_text: Take out a large frying pan and a saucepan.
steps.label: Get frying pan and saucepan
steps.notes: Retrieve the required cooking vessels before starting.

steps.raw_text: Trim the aubergine and slice it into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Place your frying pan over medium-high heat and add a generous drizzle of olive oil. Lay the aubergine slices in the pan once the oil is hot, and cook until tender and golden on both sides, about 8–10 minutes. Season both sides with salt and pepper as they cook.
steps.label: Prep and cook aubergine slices
steps.notes: Cook aubergine for 8–10 minutes until tender and golden on both sides, seasoning as they cook.

steps.raw_text: Drain the black lentils . Pour the spiced lentil sauce into your saucepan along with the lentils. Place over medium heat and cook until piping hot, around 4-5 minutes. Stir occasionally while cooking, adding a splash of water as needed if it starts to stick. Season with salt to taste.
steps.label: Cook spiced lentils in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook for 4-5 minutes until piping hot, stirring occasionally and adding water if sticking.

steps.raw_text: Wipe the frying pan you used for the aubergines and place it over medium-high heat. Warm the flatbreads by dry-frying (without oil) for 1-2 minutes, or until lightly toasted. Alternatively, you can bake or grill them in the oven until warmed through.
steps.label: Warm the flatbreads
steps.notes: Dry-fry in the wiped pan for 1-2 minutes, or warm in the oven.

steps.raw_text: Pick the mint leaves and roughly slice them.
steps.label: Pick and slice mint leaves
steps.notes: Roughly slice the picked mint leaves for garnish.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the saucy spiced lentils between serving bowls and lay the sautéed aubergine slices on top. Add dollops of garlic yoghurt , scatter over the sliced mint leaves, and serve with warm garlic & herb flatbreads on the side. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve the dish
steps.notes: Layer lentils, aubergine, garlic yoghurt, and mint; serve with warm flatbreads.

steps.label: Preheat oven and gather pans
steps.notes: Preheat to 220°C or 200°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Dice the sweet potato and aubergine into 1.5cm cubes. Add the sweet potato to one side of your roasting tray and the aubergine to the other. Drizzle generously with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and roast until tender, around 20-30 minutes.
steps.label: Dice and roast vegetables
steps.notes: Roast for 20-30 minutes until tender.

steps.raw_text: Once there's 5 minutes left on the vegetables, add the green curry soup to your saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for a further 2-3 minutes or until piping hot. Meanwhile drain and rinse the lentils well. Roll up the basil leaves with your hands and finely slice them. Set aside a quarter of the basil leaves for a garnish. Add the drained lentils and the remaining three quarters of basil to the soup and cook for a further 2 minutes. Remove from the heat, squeeze in half of the lime and season to taste with salt.
steps.label: Simmer soup and prep herbs
steps.notes: Start when 5 minutes remain on the roasting vegetables. Simmer soup 2-3 minutes, add lentils and basil, cook 2 minutes, finish with lime.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the thai green curry soup and lentils between serving bowls, arrange the sweet potato and aubergine around the bowl and garnish with the remaining basil leaves. Squeeze over the remaining lime and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish soup
steps.notes: Divide soup, arrange roasted vegetables, garnish with basil and lime.

Rich Ragu & Roasted Roots Gratin, Topped With Crispy Potato, Beetroot & Creamy Miso Bechamel

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 240°C / 220°C fan. Take out a wide, hob- and ovenproof casserole dish.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare casserole dish
equipment: wide hob- and ovenproof casserole dish
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 240°C (or 220°C fan).

steps.raw_text: Slice the cooked beetroot and sweet potato as thinly as possible, about 2mm thick. Use a mandoline if you have one to ensure even thickness. If you struggle to cut thin slices, you can microwave the sweet potato slices (3 minutes on high, covered) or parboil them in boiling water for 3 minutes to ensure they are cooked through when serving. Alternatively, you can extend the oven cooking time (see Step 4).
steps.label: Slice beetroot and sweet potato thinly
steps.notes: Slice 2mm thick. Optionally microwave for 3 minutes or parboil if slices are too thick.

steps.raw_text: In your ovenproof casserole dish, mix together the roots gratin ragu and the tin of black lentils , including the liquid from the tin. Place over medium heat and gently bring to a simmer, then turn off the heat.
steps.label: Simmer ragu and lentils in casserole
equipment: wide hob- and ovenproof casserole dish
steps.notes: Mix ragu and lentils with their liquid, bring to a simmer over medium heat, then turn off heat.

steps.raw_text: Lay the beetroot and sweet potato slices over the lentil ragu, slightly submerging them in the sauce, then drizzle over olive oil. Cover the dish with a lid or a sheet of kitchen foil and bake in the oven for 20 minutes. If the vegetables are cut into thicker slices and the microwaving or parboiling step was skipped, bake in the oven for 35 minutes instead. Once it has cooked for the above time, remove the casserole dish from the oven and pour the miso bechamel over the top. Return it to the oven and bake for a further 10 minutes without a cover, until the sauce is golden on top.
steps.label: Assemble gratin and bake in oven
equipment: wide hob- and ovenproof casserole dish
steps.notes: Bake covered for 20 minutes (or 35 minutes if slices are thick and un-microwaved), then uncovered with miso bechamel for 10 minutes.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the gratin between dishes. Finish with a sprinkle of salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Enjoy!
steps.label: Portion gratin and season to taste
steps.notes: Divide between dishes and finish with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

title: 24 Plant Frijoles Negros With Caramelised Plantain, Whipped Feta, Pink Pickled Onions, Avocado & Coriander Lime Brown Rice

steps.raw_text: Boil water in your kettle, and take out two large saucepans and a frying pan.
steps.label: Boil water and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil water in the kettle and set out two large saucepans and a frying pan.

steps.raw_text: Add boiling water from the kettle to one of the saucepans, place it over medium-high heat, and bring it to a rolling boil. Add the brown basmati rice and boil uncovered for 18-20 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite, then drain using a fine sieve. Return the rice to the pan, cover with a lid, and let it steam until the meal is ready.
steps.label: Boil and steam brown rice
steps.notes: Boil uncovered for 18-20 minutes (midpoint 19 mins) until tender with a slight bite, then drain and steam covered.

steps.raw_text: Place the other saucepan over a medium heat and add the frijole sauce and the whole tin of black beans . It is important to include the liquid from the tin, as it will add creaminess and a deep colour to the sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for a further 5 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thickened.
steps.label: Simmer black beans and sauce
steps.notes: Include the liquid from the tin for creaminess. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.

steps.raw_text: Peel, destone, and slice the avocado , then season with the juice of half a lime , salt, and pepper. Slice the remaining half of the lime into wedges. Finely chop half of the coriander including the stalks and pick the rest of the leaves for garnish.
steps.label: Prep avocado, lime, and coriander
steps.notes: Slice avocado and season with half a lime. Chop half of the coriander and pick the rest for garnish.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Peel and slice the plantain into 2cm-thick pieces, then add to the pan and fry on both sides until golden, about 2–3 minutes per side.
steps.label: Fry the sliced plantain
steps.notes: Slice plantain into 2cm-thick pieces. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.

steps.raw_text: Before serving, fluff up the brown basmati rice with a fork. Stir in a squeeze of lime juice, finely chopped coriander in the rice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
steps.label: Fluff and season rice
steps.notes: Fluff rice with a fork, stir in lime juice and chopped coriander, and season.

steps.raw_text: Divide the rice between serving bowls and ladle over the frijole sauce . Add the sautéed plantain , sliced avocado , and pink pickled onions on the side, along with a dollop of feta drizzle . Finish with a scattering of fresh coriander leaves and a squeeze of fresh lime . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve bowls
steps.notes: Assemble bowls with rice, beans, plantain, avocado, pickled onions, feta, coriander, and lime.

title: Black Bean Smash Burger Tacos With Homemade Burger Sauce & Cabbage Carrot Apple Walnut Slaw

steps.raw_text: Take out a large frying pan and two mixing bowls.
steps.label: Gather frying pan and mixing bowls
steps.notes: Retrieve one large frying pan and two mixing bowls to prepare for the recipe.

steps.raw_text: To prepare the slaw, cut and remove the core of the apple . Top and tail the carrot (peel if you prefer), and remove the hard core of the red cabbage . Julienne all of them into uniform, thin shreds (use a mandoline if you have one). Place them in one of the mixing bowls and season with the juice of half a lime , a drizzle of olive oil, and salt and pepper to taste. Roughly chop the walnuts , fold them in, and set aside. Cut the remaining lime into wedges for garnish and set aside.
steps.label: Prepare slaw and chop walnuts
steps.notes: Julienne the apple, carrot, and red cabbage. Toss with lime juice, olive oil, salt, pepper, and chopped walnuts. Set aside with lime wedges.

steps.raw_text: To prepare the burger mixture, place your frying pan over medium-low heat and dry toast (without oil) the gram flour for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it becomes golden. Drain the black beans and transfer them into the other mixing bowl. Roughly mash them with the back of a fork. Add the toasted gram flour and the patty flavour bomb , then stir well to combine.
steps.label: Toast flour and mash black beans
steps.notes: Dry toast gram flour for 2 minutes over medium-low heat until golden. Mash drained black beans and mix with toasted flour and patty flavour bomb.

steps.raw_text: Wipe clean the frying pan you used for toasting the gram flour and place it over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. While the oil heats up, divide the burger mixture and spread it on each of the flour tortillas in an even layer around 2-3mm thick. Place them on the pan with the burger mixture side down and press with a spatula and cook for 4-5 minutes until the mixture starts to caramelise. Flip it onto the other side and cook further 30-60 seconds until the tortilla is golden. Cook in a few batches depending on the size of your frying pan, adding more oil for each batch.
steps.label: Spread mixture on tortillas and fry
steps.notes: Wipe pan clean. Cook tortillas in batches over medium heat. Fry mixture-side down for 4-5 minutes until caramelised, then flip and cook for 30-60 seconds.

steps.raw_text: To serve, add a dollop of the burger sauce on each of the burger tortillas and fold them in half. Plate them up along with the slaw and lime wedges. You can either stuff the inside of the tortillas with the slaw or place it on top of the folded tacos. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble tacos and plate with slaw
steps.notes: Add burger sauce to tortillas, fold in half, and serve with the prepared slaw and lime wedges.

title: Burnt Lemon & Mustard Butter Beans With Regenerative Spelt Conchigliette, Confit Cherry Tomatoes, Cavolo Nero & Dill

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Boil your kettle and take out an ovenproof ramekin (in a size that snugly fits all the cherry tomatoes in a single layer), a griddle pan or frying pan, as well as two saucepans.
steps.label: Preheat oven and boil kettle
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Boil kettle and gather pans.

steps.raw_text: Place your cherry tomatoes in the ramekin and pour in good olive oil so the tomatoes are at least half submerged in the oil. Add a sprinkle of salt and pepper, cover tightly with a lid or foil, and place in the oven until serving. You can use less oil, but this is the technique for 'confit' cherry tomatoes and creates a flavoursome finishing oil too.
steps.label: Confit the cherry tomatoes
steps.notes: Keep tomatoes in the oven until serving.

steps.raw_text: Fill one of your saucepans with the boiling water from the kettle, add salt, and place over medium heat. Cook the spelt conchiglietti until al dente, about 10-12 minutes.
steps.label: Cook spelt conchiglietti
steps.notes: Cook until al dente, about 10-12 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Place the other saucepan over medium heat and add the creamy butter bean sauce . Drain the butter beans and add them to the sauce to gently warm through. You can adjust the consistency of the sauce to make it more brothy if you prefer, using pasta cooking water or some of the liquid from the butter bean tin.
steps.label: Warm butter beans in sauce
steps.notes: Gently warm through. Adjust consistency with pasta water if desired.

steps.raw_text: Halve the lemon and remove the hardy stems from the cavolo nero , then tear the leaves into bite-size pieces. Pick the dill leaves for garnish and set aside. Place your griddle pan or frying pan over high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, place the lemon halves cut-side down and cook until charred and caramelised, around 3-5 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside. Wipe the same pan clean with kitchen towel, add another drizzle of olive oil, then add the cavolo nero and sauté until vibrant green and crispy at the edges, about 4–5 minutes. STEP 5 Once the pasta is cooked, drain well and add it to the creamy butter bean sauce along with the sautéed cavolo nero and a squeeze from one half of the burnt lemon , then stir to combine. STEP 5 To serve, divide between serving bowls and top with the confit cherry tomatoes . Garnish with dill leaves , drizzle over some of the confit tomato oil , and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Squeeze over more burnt lemon juice to taste. Enjoy!
steps.label: Sauté greens, char lemon, and assemble
steps.notes: Char lemon for 3-5 minutes. Sauté cavolo nero for 4-5 minutes until crispy. Combine with pasta, beans, and lemon juice, then plate and garnish.

title: Butternut Squash Curried Noodles With Tenderstem Broccoli & Superseed Chilli Rayu Drizzle

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan. Take out a baking tray and a saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C for fan ovens. Gather the baking tray and saucepan.

steps.raw_text: Halve the butternut squash and remove the seeds using a spoon. Cut each half into wedges about 2 cm thick. Place them on the baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes, or until the edges start to caramelise. You may receive a particularly large butternut squash depending on the season. Around 200 g of squash flesh per person works well for this recipe, so you can save the rest for another meal. Leftover roasted butternut squash will keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days.
steps.label: Prep and roast butternut squash
steps.notes: Roast for 20 minutes until edges caramelise. Use roughly 200g of squash flesh per person.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, fill a saucepan with boiling water from the kettle and bring it back to the boil. Cook the tenderstem broccoli until vibrant green and al dente, about 3 to 4 minutes, then remove using a slotted spoon. Add the flat rice noodles to the same water and cook for 5 minutes, or until al dente. Drain and rinse well under cold running water, then leave in a colander to drain. Quickly rinse the saucepan ready for the next step.
steps.label: Cook broccoli and rice noodles
steps.notes: Cook broccoli for 3-4 minutes, then noodles for 5 minutes in the same water. Rinse the saucepan immediately after draining.

steps.raw_text: Place the saucepan back over medium heat and add the curried coconut broth along with 120 ml of water (double the amount for four portions). Gently heat until piping hot.
steps.label: Heat curried coconut broth
steps.notes: Gently heat until piping hot. Use 120ml of water for two portions, or 240ml for four portions.

steps.raw_text: Pick the coriander leaves and halve the lime , ready for garnish.
steps.label: Prep coriander and lime garnish
steps.notes: Prepare the garnish while other components are cooking.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the flat rice noodles between serving bowls and pour over the curried coconut broth . Top with the roasted butternut squash wedges and tenderstem broccoli , then drizzle over the superseed chilli crunch . Finish with a scattering of coriander leaves and a squeeze of fresh lime . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish noodle bowls
steps.notes: Layer noodles, broth, squash, broccoli, chilli crunch, coriander, and a squeeze of lime.

title: Butternut Squash & Gochujang Pasta With Garlicky Green Kale & Sunflower Seed Sprinkle
Smoky Butternut Squash & "Nduja" Lasagne With Tender Lentils & Creamy Miso Spinach Bechamel

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Take out a saucepan, a mixing bowl and a baking dish around 15x20cm (or double this for a four person box).
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C or 180°C fan. Prepare a 15x20cm baking dish.

steps.raw_text: Drain the lentils and add them to your mixing bowl along with the squash & nduja filling . Give everything a good mix to combine.
steps.label: Mix lentils and squash filling
steps.notes: Ensure lentils are well drained before mixing with the squash and nduja filling.

steps.raw_text: Place a saucepan over medium heat and add the creamy miso bechamel . Bring it to a gentle simmer, then add the baby spinach and cook for about a minute until wilted.
steps.label: Simmer bechamel and wilt spinach
steps.notes: Bring bechamel to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then cook spinach for about 1 minute until wilted.

steps.raw_text: Build your lasagne in three layers: Spread one-third of the lentils, squash & nduja mix in the base of your dish. Cover with lasag ne sheets (about 2½ sheets per layer). Top with one-third of the baby spinach & miso b echamel , then another third of the lentils, squash & nduja mix . Repeat with more lasagne sheets , another third of baby spinach & miso b echamel , and the remaining lentils, squash & nduja mix . Finish with a final layer of lasagne sheets and the rest of the baby spinach & miso b echamel . Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then bake for 25–30 minutes, until bubbling and golden. To check doneness, insert a knife into the centre, and if it’s hot through and the pasta is tender, it's ready.
steps.label: Assemble and bake the lasagne
steps.notes: Bake for 25–30 minutes (midpoint 28 mins) until bubbling and golden. Check doneness by inserting a knife into the centre to ensure it is hot and the pasta is tender.

steps.raw_text: Place the lasagne in the middle of the table and divide it between serving plates. We like stacking pieces on top of each other to make one bigger slice per person, but you could serve them as they are too. Enjoy!
steps.label: Portion and serve the lasagne
steps.notes: Divide between plates. Stacking pieces on top of each other is recommended for a larger slice.

title: Butternut Squash & Spelt Risotto With Crispy Sage & Smoky Toasted Pine Nuts

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a large saucepan, a large frying pan, and a small frying pan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather all necessary pans to streamline the cooking process.

steps.raw_text: Pour the boiling water from your kettle into the large saucepan and salt the water. Place over medium-high heat. Once the water is bubbling, add the pearled spelt and reduce to a simmer. Cook until al dente, around 20 minutes.
steps.label: Cook pearled spelt until al dente
steps.notes: Cook the spelt in salted boiling water over medium-high heat, then reduce to a simmer for around 20 minutes until al dente.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile remove the hardy stems from the cavolo nero and cut the leaves into bite-sized pieces. Once the spelt is 5 minutes from being ready, place your large frying pan over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil, and sauté the cavolo nero until tender and a little crispy at the edges, around 5 minutes. Zest half of the lemon over the cavolo nero and season with salt and pepper. Cut the lemon into wedges for garnish.
steps.label: Prep and sauté cavolo nero
steps.notes: Sauté the prepped cavolo nero for about 5 minutes over medium heat when the spelt has 5 minutes left. Finish with lemon zest, salt, and pepper.

steps.raw_text: Once the pearled spelt is cooked al dente, reserve a mug of the cooking water, then drain the spelt. Return it to the saucepan and add the butternut squash sauce . Place the saucepan back over medium heat, stirring occasionally, and cook until the sauce is bubbling. Use the reserved spelt cooking water to adjust the consistency until creamy.
steps.label: Drain spelt and add squash sauce
steps.notes: Be sure to reserve a mug of cooking water before draining. Cook with the butternut squash sauce over medium heat until bubbling, adjusting consistency with the reserved water.

steps.raw_text: Heat a few tablespoons of olive oil in your small frying pan. When hot, pick the sage leaves and add to the oil in a single layer without overlapping. The leaves will turn translucent and the oil will stop bubbling around them when they’re crisp. Turn off the heat and sprinkle in the smoky pine nut mix so it toasts slightly without burning.
steps.label: Fry sage and toast pine nuts
steps.notes: Fry sage leaves in a single layer until translucent and crisp. Turn off the heat before adding the pine nuts to prevent burning.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the risotto between serving bowls. Scatter over the crispy sage and smoky pine nuts , then drizzle with any remaining sage oil. Squeeze over the lemon juice to taste and season with salt and pepper. Serve with a side of zesty sautéed cavolo nero and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate risotto and garnish to serve
steps.notes: Divide the risotto, top with crispy sage, pine nuts, sage oil, and lemon juice. Serve alongside the sautéed cavolo nero.

title: Butternut Squash & Sage Stuffed Conchiglioni Pasta Shells In Creamy Garlic & Spinach Sauce

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan. Boil your kettle and take out a large saucepan and a wide ovenproof or casserole dish.
steps.label: Preheat oven and boil kettle
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan). Boil kettle and prepare equipment.

steps.raw_text: Place the saucepan over medium heat and pour in the boiling water from the kettle. Salt the water generously, add the conchiglioni pasta shells , and cook for 8 minutes, or until al dente. Take care not to overcook, as the pasta should remain slightly firm. This will make it easier to fill with the squash puree and it will continue cooking in the oven later. Drain well and rinse the pasta so it is cool enough to handle for filling.
steps.label: Cook and drain pasta shells
steps.notes: Cook pasta for 8 minutes until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water so they are cool enough to handle.

steps.raw_text: Pour the creamy gratin sauce into your ovenproof or casserole dish. Fold in the baby spinach and spread the mixture evenly across the base of the dish. Fill each conchiglioni shell with the squash puree using a dessert spoon, then arrange them in a single layer on top of the gratin sauce. Gently press them into the sauce so they are half submerged. Drizzle over good-quality olive oil and bake for 10–15 minutes, or until the pasta is tender and slightly crispy in places, and the squash filling is lightly golden.
steps.label: Assemble and bake stuffed pasta
steps.notes: Bake for 10–15 minutes (midpoint 13 minutes) plus 5 minutes for assembly. Bake until pasta is tender and slightly crispy, and squash filling is lightly golden.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the butternut squash & sage stuffed conchiglioni with the creamy sauce between serving plates. Finish with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and season pasta
steps.notes: Divide pasta and sauce between plates. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

title: High Protein Caesar Pasta Salad With Tempeh Pancetta, Cavolo Nero, Mangetout & Toasted Nuts & Seeds
Caprese Salad With 'Burrata', Hazelnut Pesto, Rustic Croutons & Tender Butterbeans

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C and take out a roasting tray.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare tray
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C and set aside the roasting tray.

steps.raw_text: Cut each tomato into eight pieces by quartering them and then cutting each quarter in half. Peel and finely slice half of the red onion, saving the other half for another recipe. Open, drain and rinse the butterbeans . Add the tomatoes , butterbeans and sliced onion to a large mixing bowl, toss in a healthy glug of extra virgin olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Leave to sit while you prepare the croutons, so the tomatoes release their juices.
steps.label: Prep tomatoes, onions, and butterbeans
steps.notes: Let the tomato mixture sit to release juices while preparing the croutons.

steps.raw_text: Tear the ciabatta into rough chunks and place in your roasting tray. Toss the croutons in a drizzle of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Roast for 10 minutes or until golden. Once they’re done, mix 2/3rds of them through the tomatoes in the mixing bowl.
steps.label: Prepare and roast croutons
steps.notes: Roast for 10 minutes or until golden. Mix 2/3rds of the croutons into the tomatoes.

steps.raw_text: Divide the dressed tomatoes between serving bowls and scatter over the remaining ciabatta croutons . Add a spoon of vegan 'burrata' to the middle of the bowl, then drizzle the hazelnut pesto over everything (if the pesto has thickened in the fridge you can loosen the pesto with a little olive oil or water). Season to taste with salt or pepper and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate salad and garnish
steps.notes: Loosen the pesto with olive oil or water if it has thickened in the fridge.

title: Crispy Caramelised Brussels Sprouts & Parsnips With Farro, Tangy Caper Salsa Verde & Toasted Hazelnuts

steps.raw_text: This is one of very few recipes that takes a little longer than 15 minutes, but we hope you'll forgive us when you see how easy it is to finish!
steps.label: Read recipe introduction
steps.notes: Introductory step noting that the recipe takes slightly longer than 15 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, pre-heat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, then take out a large roasting tray and a saucepan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and preheat oven
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Slice off and discard the bottom end of the brussels sprouts , then slice vertically in half. Cut the parsnip into 1.5cm cubes. Add the parsnips to your roasting tray, toss in a drizzle of olive oil, season well with salt and pepper and roast for 10 minutes. Then add the brussels sprouts tossed in oil, salt and pepper and roast for a further 15-20 minutes or until golden and caramelised. Add the hazelnuts to one side of your baking tray for the final 5 minutes of cooking time.
steps.label: Prep and roast vegetables
steps.notes: Roast parsnips for 10 minutes, add sprouts for 15-20 minutes (midpoint 17.5) until golden, and add hazelnuts for the final 5 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, pour boiling water from your kettle into your saucepan and place over a medium heat. Add the farro and boil for 15 minute or until tender but al dente.
steps.label: Boil the farro
steps.notes: Boil farro for 15 minutes or until tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the brussels sprouts , parsnips and farro between serving plates, scatter over the toasted hazelnuts , then smother everything generously in tangy caper salsa verde dressing. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve
steps.notes: Divide sprouts, parsnips, and farro, scatter hazelnuts, and top with tangy caper salsa verde.

title: Comforting Slow-Cooked Caribbean Jackfruit Curry With Coconut Rice & Braised Cavolo Nero

steps.notes: Marinate the jackfruit with garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet, allspice, and curry powder.

steps.raw_text: cooked slowly with fresh vegetables and kidney beans until juicy and tender

steps.notes: Slowly cook the marinated jackfruit with fresh vegetables and kidney beans until juicy and tender.

steps.raw_text: fluffy coconut rice
steps.label: Cook the coconut rice
steps.notes: Cook the basmati rice with desiccated coconut until fluffy.

steps.raw_text: Braised Cavolo Nero
steps.label: Braise the cavolo nero

steps.raw_text: Served with fluffy coconut rice and vitamin-rich cavolo nero.

title: Crispy Cauliflower Al Pastor Tacos With Jalapeño Salsa, Chipotle Cashew Crema, Pickled Cabbage & Lime

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 220°C fan, then take out a large roasting tray and a frying pan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat to 200°C or 220°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized chunks, place them in the roasting tray, and toss with a drizzle of olive oil and the adobo sauce , ensuring each piece is evenly coated. Roast in the oven for 15–20 minutes, or until the sauce starts to caramelise.
steps.label: Prep and roast cauliflower
steps.notes: Roast for 15–20 minutes (midpoint 17.5 minutes) until sauce caramelises.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and dry-fry the corn tacos (without oil) for 30 seconds on each side, or until warm and soft. Add a sprinkle of water if you’d like them extra soft. Alternatively, place the stack of tacos on a plate and cover with a damp kitchen towel. Microwave on medium for 30 seconds at a time; after about a minute, the tacos should be soft and fragrant.
steps.label: Warm the corn tacos
steps.notes: Dry-fry for 30 seconds per side or microwave for about 1 minute.

steps.raw_text: Cut the lime into quarters and drain the red wine vinegar pickled red cabbage .
steps.label: Prep lime and cabbage
steps.notes: Cut lime into quarters and drain the pickled cabbage.

steps.raw_text: To serve, lay the tacos on a large plate and top with the pickled red cabbage and roasted cauliflower . Drizzle over the jalapeno salsa and cashew crema , then finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve tacos
steps.notes: Top tacos with cabbage, cauliflower, salsa, crema, and lime juice.

title: Cauliflower & Broccoli 'Cheese' With Golden Garlic Hazelnut Breadcrumbs and Herby Gremolata Dressing
Charred Aubergine With Romesco, Bulgar Wheat Pilaf, Tahini Sauce & Herby Caper Gremolata

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a large roasting tray, and a saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan). Get out the roasting tray and saucepan.

steps.raw_text: Slice the aubergine into rounds, about 1cm thick. We recommend roasting the aubergine for better flavour, but it does take longer. If you want the meal ready within 15 minutes, simply fry the aubergine with a healthy drizzle of olive oil in a medium-hot frying pan for 5-7 minutes on each side until golden and tender. Otherwise, if you're happy to wait 30 mins, lay the aubergine rounds on a baking tray, brush with olive oil on both sides, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins, then flip the aubergines and roast for another 10-15 mins until softened and golden. Alternatively, if you have an air fryer, you could air fry them for 15 minutes, flipping halfway. You could also turn the chickpeas into crispy chickpeas by draining, patting dry and then roasting or air frying the chickpeas in oil, salt and pepper for the same amount of time as the aubergine (optional, but recommended!).
steps.label: Slice and cook aubergine
steps.notes: Roasting takes 25-30 mins (flip halfway). Frying takes 10-14 mins total. Air frying takes 15 mins. Optionally roast/air fry chickpeas too.

steps.raw_text: Place the bulgur wheat in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and then turn down to a simmer and cook until tender but al dente, around 6-8 minutes. If you haven't roasted the chickpeas, simply drain and add these to the bulgur wheat pan for the final one minute of cooking time. Stir 2 tbsp of the herby caper gremolata through the bulgur wheat and season well with salt and pepper. This is your bulgur and chickpea pilaf.
steps.label: Cook bulgur wheat and mix pilaf
steps.notes: Simmer bulgur for 6-8 minutes. Add drained chickpeas for the final minute if not roasted. Stir in 2 tbsp gremolata.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spread half of the romesco sauce (cold) onto the bottom of each plate, top with the bulgur pilaf , then with the aubergine and finish with the tahini drizzle and remaining herby caper gremolata . If you made crispy chickpeas, scatter these over at the end. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the dish
steps.notes: Layer romesco, bulgur pilaf, aubergine, tahini drizzle, gremolata, and optional crispy chickpeas.

title: Charred Courgettes With Romesco, Chickpeas, Giant Cous Cous, Tahini Sauce & Mint Pesto

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, pre-heat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a large roasting tray, a small frying pan and a saucepan.
steps.label: Boil kettle, preheat oven, and gather equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan while kettle boils.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and add the almonds . Dry fry (without oil) for 3-4 minutes or until nicely toasted, tossing occasionally so they don't burn. Set aside and roughly chop or crush the almonds by pressing down on them with a rolling pin or bottom of a heavy pan.
steps.label: Toast and crush the almonds
steps.notes: Dry fry for 3-4 minutes until toasted, tossing occasionally. Crush with a rolling pin or heavy pan.

steps.raw_text: Cut the courgette in half lengthways, then into large, diagonal pieces. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper, then place on your roasting tray. Cook for 15 minutes or until the courgette is caramelised and starting to char.
steps.label: Prep and roast the courgettes
steps.notes: Roast for 15 minutes until caramelised and starting to char.

steps.raw_text: Fill your saucepan with boiling water and place over a high heat. Once it's bubbling, reduce to a simmer and add the giant cous cous . Cook until tender but al dente, around 6-8 minutes. Drain the chickpeas then add them to the pan for the final one minute of cooking time.
steps.label: Cook giant couscous and chickpeas
steps.notes: Cook couscous for 6-8 minutes, adding drained chickpeas for the final 1 minute.

steps.raw_text: Drain the giant cous cous and chickpeas . Add them to a bowl along with the cooked courgettes and mix through half of the mint pesto .
steps.label: Mix couscous, chickpeas, courgettes, and pesto
steps.notes: Drain couscous and chickpeas, then mix with cooked courgettes and half of the mint pesto.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spread the romesco sauce (cold) at the bottom of a plate and top with the chickpeas , couscous and courgettes . Drizzle over the remaining mint pesto and tahini sauce , and sprinkle the toasted almonds to finish. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate, drizzle sauces, and garnish with almonds
steps.notes: Spread cold romesco sauce first, top with the warm mixture, drizzle remaining pesto and tahini, and finish with almonds.

title: Charred Gochujang Glazed Hispi Cabbage Over Lime Tahini Yoghurt With Lentils & Orange Peanut Crumb

steps.raw_text: Pre-heat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, then take out a large frying pan and two baking trays.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan. Retrieve one large frying pan and two baking trays.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan on the hob over a high heat. Cut the hispi cabbage in half length-ways, then again length-ways into quarters. Rub each quarter with olive oil and a little salt and pepper. Once your pan is searing hot, char the cabbage cut side down, until each of the two cut sides of the wedges are starting to blacken a little, around 5 minutes.
steps.label: Prep and char hispi cabbage
steps.notes: Cut cabbage into quarters, oil and season, then char cut side down in a hot pan for around 5 minutes until blackened.

steps.raw_text: Drain the lentils and transfer them to one of your baking trays. Season with a little drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper, then spread them evenly in a thin layer. Place the charred cabbage wedges on the other baking tray, cut side up. Put both trays in the oven and roast for 15 minutes. About halfway through, remove the cabbage wedges and brush the cut sides with the gochujang sauce . Towards the end of the cooking time, you may want to baste the cabbage a couple of times to ensure the sauce seeps into the layers and caramelises on top.
steps.label: Roast lentils and cabbage
steps.notes: Roast lentils and cabbage on separate trays for 15 minutes. Brush cabbage with gochujang sauce halfway through and baste towards the end.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile finely chop the chives for garnish.
steps.label: Finely chop the chives
steps.notes: Finely chop the chives for garnish while other components cook.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spoon the lime tahini yoghurt onto two plates and top with the lentils . Place two pieces of hispi cabbage wedges onto each plate and drizzle with any leftover gochujang sauce from the baking tray . Finish with the chopped chives and orange peanut crumb . Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the dish
steps.notes: Layer yoghurt, lentils, and cabbage. Drizzle with leftover sauce and finish with chives and orange peanut crumb.

title: Charred Miso Glazed Hispi Cabbage Over Tahini Yoghurt With Crispy Chickpeas & Superseed Chilli Crunch

steps.raw_text: charred hispi cabbage
steps.label: Char the hispi cabbage
steps.notes: Char the cabbage until it has smoky, charred edges and a sweet, nutty flavour.

steps.raw_text: layered over silky tahini yoghurt with plump chickpeas
steps.label: Prepare and layer tahini yoghurt and chickpeas
steps.notes: Layer the silky tahini yoghurt and plump chickpeas on the serving plate.

steps.raw_text: finished with a zingy, herby zhoug dressing and a scattering of spiced toasted dukkah
steps.label: Garnish and finish the dish
steps.notes: Top the layered cabbage with the zhoug dressing and a scattering of spiced toasted dukkah.

title: Charred Hispi Cabbage Over Golden Daal With Organic Soy Yoghurt, Tamarind & Date Chutney, Toasted Almonds & Coriander

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a saucepan and an ovenproof skillet - if you don't have an ovenproof one, take out a frying pan and baking tray instead.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan. Prepare saucepan and skillet or frying pan and baking tray.

steps.raw_text: Place your skillet or frying pan over a high heat. Add the flaked almonds and dry fry (without oil) until toasted. Set aside and wipe the pan clean with some kitchen towel.
steps.label: Toast flaked almonds in skillet
steps.notes: Dry fry almonds without oil over high heat until toasted, then wipe pan clean.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, cut the hispi cabbage into quarters lengthways and rub with a generous amount of olive oil. Season well with salt and pepper. Using the same pan you toasted the almonds in, place the hispi cabbage cut side down and fry until nicely charred on high heat. Turn and repeat on the other cut side. Turn the heat off, then place the cabbage quarters onto their backs so the cut sides are facing upwards. Transfer the pan to the oven and roast until tender in the centre and charred around the edges, about 15 minutes.
steps.label: Prep, char, and roast hispi cabbage
steps.notes: Char cabbage on both cut sides, then roast in the oven for about 15 minutes until tender.

steps.raw_text: Add the daal sauce , red lentils and 200ml of water to your other saucepan and cook for 10-15 mins until the lentils are soft and tender. Stir occasionally while cooking and add more water as needed if it reduces too much or starts to stick. Season to taste with salt.
steps.label: Simmer daal and lentils in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook for 10-15 minutes (midpoint 13 mins) until lentils are soft. Stir occasionally and add water if needed.

steps.raw_text: Finely slice the red chilli and roughly chop the coriander .
steps.label: Slice red chilli and chop coriander
steps.notes: Finely slice the chilli and roughly chop the coriander while other components cook.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the daal between serving bowls, top with the charred hispi cabbage and drizzle over the date tamarind chutney, soy yoghurt , some chopped coriander and sliced red chilli . Season to taste with salt and pepper and enjoy! Please note: although the dates in the date tamarind chutney are carefully pitted, there is a very small possibility of traces of stones
steps.label: Assemble daal, cabbage, and garnishes
steps.notes: Divide daal, top with cabbage, drizzle chutney and yoghurt, and garnish. Note: watch out for potential date stones in the chutney.

title: Cheats Aubergine & Lentil Parmigiana With Creamy Miso Bechamel & Seasonal Salad Tossed In Vinaigrette

steps.raw_text: Take out a large ovenproof casserole dish and one mixing bowl, and preheat your oven to 200°C /180°C fan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare dishes
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C (or 180°C fan).

steps.raw_text: Trim the top and end of the aubergine , then slice it lengthways into 1.5cm thick slices.
steps.label: Trim and slice aubergine
steps.notes: Slice lengthways into 1.5cm thick slices.

steps.raw_text: Place the casserole dish over medium-high heat and add a generous drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the aubergine slices, season with salt, and sauté until tender in the centre and lightly golden on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove the aubergine from the pan and set aside.
steps.label: Sauté the aubergine slices
steps.notes: Sauté for 4-5 minutes per side until tender in the centre and lightly golden.

steps.raw_text: Drain the brown lentils and add them to the casserole dish along with the tomato sauce . Place the casserole dish over a medium heat and cook until the sauce is bubbling. Arrange the aubergine slices in the casserole so they are evenly distributed in the sauce. Push them down so they are partly submerged beneath the sauce but with some edges still sitting above the surface, so that they crisp up a little when baked. Pour the miso bechamel over the top, then place the dish into the oven and bake for 15 minutes or until the bechamel has thickened and browned a little on top.
steps.label: Assemble and bake the parmigiana
steps.notes: Bake for 15 minutes or until the bechamel has thickened and browned on top.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, toss the mixed leaf salad with the french vinaigrette and season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
steps.label: Toss and season the salad
steps.notes: Toss mixed leaves with vinaigrette and season to taste.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the aubergine parmigiana between serving bowls and add a side of mixed leaf salad . Enjoy!
steps.label: Portion and serve the meal
steps.notes: Divide the parmigiana and salad between serving bowls.

title: Chickpea 'Tuna' Sushi Bowl With Crunchy Sesame Slaw, Creamy Avocado & Zingy Ginger Soy Dressing
High Protein Chilli Garlic Tempeh Noodles With Crunchy Rainbow Vegetables & Toasted Sesame Seeds

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a sauce pan and a deep frying pan or wok.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather a saucepan and a deep frying pan or wok.

steps.raw_text: Fill your saucepan with boiling water from the kettle and place it over medium heat. Once the water is bubbling, add the udo n noodles and cook for 5-6 minutes, or until al dente. Drain and rinse well under cold running water, then leave them in a colander to drain.
steps.label: Cook and drain udon noodles
steps.notes: Cook noodles for 5-6 minutes until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.raw_text: Julienne the carrot and finely slice the red cabbage (a mandolin can be helpful if you have one) and pak choi . Finely slice the spring onions , keeping the green and white parts separate. This is all your veg prep done.
steps.label: Prep and slice vegetables
steps.notes: Julienne carrot, slice cabbage and pak choi. Keep green and white parts of spring onions separate.

steps.raw_text: Crumble the tempeh into small, bite-sized pieces. Place a frying pan or wok over medium-high heat and add a generous drizzle of neutral oil. Fry the crumbled tempeh for 6-8 minutes, until it starts to brown and turn crispy at the edges. Stir in one-third of the chili garlic tempeh sauce and make sure all the tempeh pieces are evenly coated. Set aside and keep warm.
steps.label: Crumble and fry tempeh
steps.notes: Fry crumbled tempeh for 6-8 minutes (midpoint 7) until crispy, coat with 1/3 of sauce, and keep warm.

steps.raw_text: Wipe clean or quickly rinse the frying pan or wok used for the tempeh if there are any burnt bits at the bottom. Place it back over medium-high heat and add another drizzle of neutral oil. Add the prepared carrot, red cabbage , pak choi , and the white part of the spring onions , then stir-fry for 5 minutes. Add the drained udon noodles along with the remaining chili garlic tempeh sauce , tossing everything to make sure it's well combined and evenly coated in the sauce. Add a splash of water if needed to prevent burning or sticking, and season to taste with salt or a splash of soy sauce (optional). STEP 5 To serve, divide the noodles between serving bowls, top with the tempeh and then garnish with the green spring onions and a sprinkle of sesame garnish . Enjoy!
steps.label: Stir-fry, combine, and serve
steps.notes: Stir-fry vegetables for 5 minutes, toss with noodles and remaining sauce, then plate and garnish.

title: Smokey Black Bean Chilli With House Pickles, Coconut Yoghurt & Tostada Dippers

steps.raw_text: three bean chilli is layered with a multitude of complex flavours like cumin, allspice, cinnamon and chilli
steps.label: Cook three bean chilli
steps.notes: Simmer the medley of beans (kidney, cannellini, black), onion, carrot, walnuts, and plum tomatoes with soy sauce, water, and spices (cumin, allspice, cinnamon, chilli, oregano).

steps.raw_text: basmati rice
steps.label: Cook basmati rice
steps.notes: Cook the basmati rice in water.

steps.raw_text: citrusy pickled slaw
steps.label: Prepare pickled slaw
steps.notes: Combine cabbage, carrot, apple cider vinegar, salt, and raw natural cane sugar to create the pickled slaw.

steps.raw_text: crispy corn tortilla dippers
steps.label: Prepare corn tortilla dippers
steps.notes: Prepare crispy corn tortilla dippers using the white corn tacos.

steps.raw_text: served with crispy corn tortilla dippers... offset by cooling coconut yoghurt
steps.label: Assemble and serve
steps.notes: Serve the hot three bean chilli over basmati rice, topped with the cooling coconut yoghurt, citrusy pickled slaw, and crispy corn tortilla dippers.

title: Charred Cauliflower Steaks With Chimichurri, Pine Nuts & Pomegranate Seeds Over Creamy Butterbean Mash

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a large roasting tray and a small saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat to 220°C or 200°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Remove any tough or damaged outer leaves from the cauliflower . Using a large knife, trim the base and cut the cauliflower into quarters, keeping the leaves intact. Rub some olive oil, salt, pepper and drizzle over the smoky cauliflower marinad e . Use your hands or a brush to spread the marinade and seasoning all over the cauliflower. Place on your roasting tray and roast in the oven for 20-30 minutes or until it's browning/blackening on the outside and tender but al dente in the centre.
steps.label: Prep and roast cauliflower
steps.notes: Roast for 20-30 minutes until browning/blackening and tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, drain the butter beans and add them to a blender with half of the lemon tahini dressing . Blend to a smooth puree (you may need to add a little water if it's too thick). Alternatively if you don't have a blender, you can mash the beans with a fork or potato masher for a chunkier texture. When there's 5 minutes left on the cauliflower, add the tahini butterbean mash to your saucepan and warm through over a medium heat until piping hot, around 3-5 minutes. If it starts to stick, you may need to add water as you cook to loosen. Season generously with salt and pepper to taste.
steps.label: Blend and warm butterbean mash
steps.notes: Warm mash for 3-5 minutes when cauliflower has 5 minutes left. Add water if it sticks.

steps.raw_text: Place your small frying pan over medium heat, and dry toast the pine nuts until golden.
steps.label: Toast the pine nuts
steps.notes: Dry toast over medium heat until golden.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spread the creamy butter bean mash onto a large plate and place the cauliflower steaks on top. Drizzle over the chimichurri dressing and the remaining lemon tahini dressing . Scatter with pomegranate seeds and toasted pine nuts , and finish with a drizzle of good-quality olive oil (optional). Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the dish
steps.notes: Layer mash, cauliflower, dressings, seeds, and nuts. Finish with optional olive oil.

title: Chinese Pancakes With Crispy Pulled Oyster Mushrooms, Date Hoi Sin, Fresh Cucumber & Spring Onions

steps.raw_text: Take out a large non-stick frying pan and set a steamer over the hob if you don't have a microwave for warming the pancakes.
steps.label: Set up pan and steamer
steps.notes: Set up the steamer over the hob if you do not plan to use a microwave for warming the pancakes.

steps.raw_text: Use your hands to pull apart the oyster mushrooms into thin strips. Place the cornstarch into a large bowl, season well with salt and pepper, then add the oyster mushrooms and give them a good mix so until coated evenly. Place your non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, fry the oyster mushrooms in batches until golden and crispy, around 10-15 minutes. Make sure you fry in batches leaving space between the mushrooms, otherwise they won't crisp up. If they stick together as you cook, break them up regularly, using two forks. Keep frying until they're all golden and crispy on all sides. Season the mushrooms with sea salt to taste.
steps.label: Prep and fry oyster mushrooms
steps.notes: Frying takes 10-15 minutes. Fry in batches to ensure they get crispy, and use two forks to break them apart if they stick.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, finely slice the spring onions lengthways (including the green bits!) and cut the cucumber into matchsticks. Julienne the carrot , or you can use a vegetable peeler to make ribbons. Pierce the film packet the pancakes are in, then place in your steamer for 4-5 minutes or microwave on a low heat for 30 seconds.
steps.label: Prep vegetables and warm pancakes
steps.notes: Can be done while mushrooms are frying. Steaming takes 4-5 minutes, while microwaving takes 30 seconds.

steps.raw_text: Divide the pancakes between serving plates, then load them up with a hoisin sauce and crispy oyster mushrooms . Finish with a garnish of spring onion , cucumber and carrot . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish pancakes
steps.notes: Assemble immediately while the pancakes and mushrooms are still warm.

title: Chipotle Black Bean Burrito Bowl With Roasted Sweet Potato, Avocado, Salsa Roja, Lime Crema & Tortilla Dippers

steps.raw_text: Take out two saucepans, a large and a small roasting tray. Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan.
steps.label: Prepare equipment and preheat oven
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C or 180°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Cut the sweet potato into 1.5cm cubes and add to your large roasting tray. Toss through a drizzle of oil and season well with salt and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes or until tender. Alternatively, air fry for 20 minutes, shaking the tray every 5 minutes for an even cook.
steps.label: Prep and roast sweet potato
steps.notes: Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender, or air fry for 20 minutes shaking every 5 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Place the rice into one of your saucepans and cover with 2.5x its volume in water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover and continue to cook for 8-10 minutes or until tender but al dente. Drain and set aside to keep warm.
steps.label: Boil and cook the rice
steps.notes: Cook for 8-10 minutes until tender but al dente, then drain.

steps.raw_text: Use scissors or a knife to cut the fresh corn tortillas into triangles, place into your smaller baking tray and drizzle or brush them with a little olive oil. Once the sweet potato has had 5 minutes, bake the corn tortillas for the final 10 minutes of cooking time until perfectly crispy, turning halfway through. Season with a little salt and pepper.
steps.label: Prep and bake tortilla dippers
steps.notes: Bake for 10 minutes, starting after the sweet potato has been roasting for 5 minutes. Turn halfway.

steps.raw_text: Drain the beans and add them into your other saucepan along with the chipotle sauce and 1 tbsp of extra virgin olive oil and warm them through, around 5 minutes. Season well with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Warm the chipotle black beans
steps.notes: Warm through for around 5 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Cut the avocado in half and scoop out the flesh. Slice it thinly.
steps.label: Slice the fresh avocado
steps.notes: Slice thinly just before serving to prevent browning.

steps.raw_text: To serve, add the rice , beans , sweet potato and avocado into two bowls. Spoon over the salsa roja , lime crema and serve the crispy tortilla chips on the side.
steps.label: Assemble and serve burrito bowls
steps.notes: Divide rice, beans, sweet potato, and avocado into bowls. Top with salsa roja, lime crema, and serve with tortilla chips.

title: Chocolate, Hazelnut & Sea Salt Snack Bar - 100% Raw Whole Foods
Courgette Gratin With Cashew Cheese Sauce, Creamy Cannellini Beans And Olive & Almond Gremolata

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a wide hob- and oven-proof casserole dish or deep ovenproof pan, along with a roasting tray.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
equipment: wide hob- and oven-proof casserole dish
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan). Prepare casserole dish/pan and roasting tray.

steps.raw_text: Drain and rinse the cannellini beans and add half of it along with the creamy gratin sauce to your casserole dish and place over medium low heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Spread the rest of the cannellini beans on a roasting tray and stir through a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Prepare beans and simmer sauce
steps.notes: Drain and rinse beans. Simmer half with sauce in casserole; toss rest with oil, salt, and pepper on roasting tray.

steps.raw_text: Slice both the green courgette and yellow courgette into thin rounds, about 2mm thick. Use a mandoline if you have one to get even slices for the best result. Add about ⅓ to half of them into the simmering gratin sauce, and lay the rest in an even single layer on top. Gently press them into the sauce. Drizzle over some olive oil and place in the oven to bake for 15-20minutes until the top is golden and courgette is cooked. Use a knife to check the doneness before removing from the oven. Place the tray of seasoned cannellini beans into the oven at the same time. They should become golden and crispy in 15-20min.
steps.label: Slice courgettes and bake gratin
steps.notes: Bake gratin and beans for 15-20 minutes (midpoint 18 mins) until golden. Check doneness with a knife.

steps.raw_text: Season the rocket with half of the olive & almond gremolata and - when they're ready - stir through the crispy roasted cannellini beans.
steps.label: Season rocket and mix beans
steps.notes: Stir crispy roasted beans into rocket seasoned with half of the gremolata once they are ready.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the courgette gratin between serving dishes and drizzle over the rest of the olive & almond gremolata . Add the rocket salad to the side and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve the gratin
steps.notes: Divide gratin, drizzle remaining gremolata, and serve with rocket salad on the side.

title: Creamy Butter Beans With Burnt Lemon & Mustard Sauce, Wilted Greens, Charred Cauliflower & Green Olive Salsa

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a baking tray and a deep frying pan or wok.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Place the cauliflower in your baking tray, drizzle with some olive oil and season generously with salt and black pepper. Roast for 15-18 mins, shaking halfway through.
steps.label: Roast the cauliflower
steps.notes: Roast for 15-18 minutes, shaking the tray halfway through.

steps.raw_text: Next, char the lemon . Place your frying pan over a medium-high heat and slice the lemon in half. Once the pan is hot, place the lemon cut side down into the pan and fry for 2-3 minutes or until golden and charred. Remove and set to the side. Clean the pan if needed (some light browning is OK, but if there’s lots of residual burn it will affect the flavour of the sauce).
steps.label: Char the lemon halves
steps.notes: Fry cut side down for 2-3 minutes until golden and charred. Clean pan afterwards if needed.

steps.raw_text: Remove the stems from the cavolo nero , then chop the leaves into bite sized pieces and add these to the hot pan with a little salt and olive oil. Stir fry on medium heat for 2-3 minutes until it has darkened and has begun to wilt. Drain the butter beans , reserving all of the liquid. Add the butter beans and the lemon & mustard sauce to the pan with the cavolo nero and bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the beans and greens have softened. Gradually add the reserved bean liquid while the sauce simmers, until you reach a creamy consistency. Squeeze in the juice from one half of the burnt lemon to finish.
steps.label: Cook greens and butter beans
steps.notes: Stir fry greens for 2-3 minutes, then simmer beans for 3-4 minutes. Reserve bean liquid to adjust consistency.

steps.raw_text: To serve, ladle the creamy beans into serving bowls, top with the roasted cauliflower and green olive salsa . We recommend squeezing over the other half of lemon but you can omit this if you feel the dish has enough acidity for your preference. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve
steps.notes: Ladle beans, top with cauliflower and green olive salsa. Squeeze remaining lemon if desired.

title: Creamy Butter Beans With Caramelised Leeks, Charred Courgettes, Drizzled With Olive & Almond Pesto

steps.raw_text: Take out a saucepan and a large frying pan.
steps.label: Gather saucepan and frying pan
steps.notes: Prepare the necessary cooking vessels before starting.

steps.raw_text: Finely slice the courgette into rounds approximately 5mm thick. Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan and add the courgette slices in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes, then turn and continue cooking for a further 4–5 minutes until softened and charred. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. You may need to do this in a couple of batches, or use two pans if your pan is not large enough.
steps.label: Slice and char the courgettes
steps.notes: Slice courgettes to 5mm. Cook 3-4 minutes undisturbed, then 4-5 minutes after turning. May require batches.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, empty the caramelised leek broth and the tin of butter beans (including the water) into your saucepan and cook over a medium heat until piping hot, around 3-5 minutes. Add a splash of water if you prefer a more brothy consistency. Season to your taste with salt and plenty of pepper.
steps.label: Heat butter beans and broth
steps.notes: Cook over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot. Adjust consistency with water if desired.

steps.raw_text: To serve, ladle the beans into two bowls. Top with the charred courgette and olive pesto . Finish with a little lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice . Enjoy!
steps.label: Ladle beans and top with courgettes
steps.notes: Assemble by layering beans, charred courgettes, olive pesto, lemon zest, and lemon juice.

title: Creamy Cauliflower & Aubergine Korma With Toasted Cashews, Fresh Coriander & Rice

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan, boil your kettle, then take out a roasting tray, frying pan and saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C (or 180°C fan) and boil the kettle.

steps.raw_text: Cut the aubergine into 1.5cm cubes and place them along with the cauliflower florets into your roasting tray, toss in a drizzle of oil and season well with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes or until tender and beginning to char.
steps.label: Chop and roast aubergine and cauliflower
steps.notes: Roast for 15 minutes or until tender and beginning to char.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat, then add the cashews to toast for around 2-3 minutes. Remove and set aside.
steps.label: Toast cashews in frying pan
steps.notes: Toast for 2-3 minutes over medium heat, then set aside.

steps.raw_text: Place the basmati rice into your saucepan and cover with 2.5x its volume in boiling water from your kettle. Cook over a medium heat until tender but al dente, around 8-10 minutes.
steps.label: Cook basmati rice in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook for 8-10 minutes until tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: Once the cauliflower and aubergine are cooked, combine in your frying pan along with the korma sauce and cook until piping hot, around 2-3 minutes. Meanwhile, roughly chop the coriander leaves.
steps.label: Combine vegetables with korma sauce
steps.notes: Cook for 2-3 minutes until piping hot. Chop coriander meanwhile.

steps.raw_text: Divide the cauliflower and aubergine korma and rice between serving bowls, garnish with the toasted cashews and a scattering of fresh coriander . Enjoy
steps.label: Plate and garnish the korma
steps.notes: Garnish with toasted cashews and fresh coriander.

title: Creamy Coconut Daal With Spice Roasted Cauliflower, Crispy Kale & Coconut Yoghurt

steps.raw_text: Preheat the oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, then take out a large roasting tray and two saucepans.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat to 220°C or 200°C fan. Prepare roasting tray and two saucepans.

steps.raw_text: Cut any larger pieces of cauliflower so they're all roughly 1.5-2cm squared in size. Place into your roasting tray, add a drizzle of oil, season with the spice mix (add half if you don't like too much spice!), salt and pepper and give everything a good toss to coat. Roast for 15-20 minutes or until golden and tender.
steps.label: Chop and roast cauliflower
steps.notes: Roast for 15-20 minutes (midpoint 18) or until golden and tender.

steps.raw_text: Add the daal sauce , red lentils and 300ml of water to your other saucepan and cook for 10-15 mins until the lentils are soft and tender. Stir occasionally while cooking and add a splash of water as needed if it reduces too much or starts to stick. Season to taste with salt.
steps.label: Simmer the daal sauce
steps.notes: Cook for 10-15 minutes (midpoint 13) until lentils are soft. Stir occasionally.

steps.raw_text: Remove any hardy stems from the cavolo nero then chop into bitesized pieces. Once the cauliflower has had 10 minutes in the oven, add the kale to one side of the roasting tray, toss in a little oil, season with salt and roast for the final 5 minutes of cooking time, or until the kale is nice and crispy.
steps.label: Chop and roast cavolo nero
steps.notes: Add to the roasting tray after cauliflower has cooked for 10 minutes. Roast for the final 5 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Place the rice in a small saucepan and cover with 2x its volume in water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and cover. Allow to cook for a further 8-10 minutes or until tender.
steps.label: Boil and cook rice
steps.notes: Bring to boil, then simmer covered for 8-10 minutes (midpoint 9) until tender.

steps.raw_text: Divide the daal between serving bowls, top with crispy cavolo nero , roasted cauliflower , a squeeze of fresh lime juice and a dollop of creamy coconut yoghurt . Serve alongside your fluffy rice and enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve daal
steps.notes: Divide daal, top with roasted cauliflower, crispy kale, lime juice, and coconut yoghurt. Serve with rice.

title: Creamy Gochujang Tofu Bowl With Wakame Cucumber Pickle, Avocado, Sesame Gochugaru & Nori Snacks
Creamy Green Goddess Beans & Courgettes With Organic Cultured Yoghurt, Pistachio Za'atar & Flatbread

steps.raw_text: Take out a deep frying pan and a second wide frying pan.
steps.label: Prepare the frying pans
steps.notes: Retrieve one deep frying pan and one wide frying pan.

steps.raw_text: Place a frying pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. While it heats, finely slice the courgette , and add to the pan with a pinch of salt and fry for 8 minutes, or until softened. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans, then add them to the pan along with the green goddess sauce. In a blender, or in a bowl with a hand blender, blend the baby spinach with 50ml of water (double the amount for a 4-person portion) until smooth, then add it to the sauce and beans. We send the spinach separately to ensure the beautiful vibrant green sauce colour, but if don’t have a blender, you can finely chop the spinach instead. Stir everything together and cook for a few minutes until heated through.
steps.label: Cook courgettes, beans, and spinach sauce
steps.notes: Fry sliced courgettes for 8 minutes until softened. Blend spinach with 50ml water (or finely chop if no blender). Stir everything together and cook for a few minutes until heated through.

steps.raw_text: Add a generous drizzle of olive oil (we recommend a 2 tablespoons, but you could use less) to your other frying pan, along with the pistachio and za'atar . Heat until the nuts are lightly toasted, around 2-3 minutes. Watch carefully to ensure it doesn't burn. Remove all of the oil, nuts and spices from the pan and place into a ramekin or small bowl. Toast the flatbread in the pan for a few minutes to warm through, then cut into quarters.
steps.label: Toast pistachios and warm flatbread
steps.notes: Toast nuts and za'atar for 2-3 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning. Transfer to a ramekin, then toast flatbread in the same pan for a few minutes and cut into quarters.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the creamy green goddess beans between serving bowls, then garnish with a few dollops of yoghurt and the pistachio and za'atar drizzle . Serve the flatbread alongside to scoop it up. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate beans and garnish with yoghurt
steps.notes: Divide the green goddess beans into bowls, garnish with dollops of yoghurt and the pistachio za'atar drizzle, and serve with flatbread.

title: Creamy Kimchi Macaroni With Roasted Broccoli & Garlic Panko Breadcrumbs

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle and preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Take out a large saucepan, a small frying pan and a roasting tray.
steps.label: Boil kettle and preheat oven
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C (or 180°C fan).

steps.raw_text: Cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces. Lay them on a baking tray in a single layer with a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 10-15 mins until golden, tossing once.
steps.label: Prep and roast broccoli
steps.notes: Roast for 10-15 minutes (midpoint 13) until golden, tossing once.

steps.raw_text: Pour boiling water into your saucepan, add the macaroni pasta, then place over the heat and salt the water well. Boil the pasta for 8 minutes or until al dente. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain and return the pasta to the pan.
steps.label: Boil the macaroni pasta
steps.notes: Boil for 8 minutes or until al dente. Remember to scoop out a mug of pasta water before draining.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over medium heat, and dry fry (without oil) the garlic breadcrumbs mix until lightly toasted. Finely chop the spring onion and keep the white half separate from the green. Chop the vegan kimchi into smaller bite-sized pieces (don’t throw away the juices as they’re packed with flavour and probiotics!).
steps.label: Toast breadcrumbs and chop aromatics
steps.notes: Dry fry breadcrumbs until lightly toasted. Keep spring onion whites and greens separate. Do not discard kimchi juices.

steps.raw_text: Add the gochujang 'cheese' sa uce , spring onion whites, and kimchi to the pot with the macaroni and stir to heat through. Add a few splashes of pasta water as needed to make the sauce silky. Add the cooked broccoli and stir again until just combined.
steps.label: Combine pasta, sauce, and broccoli
steps.notes: Stir to heat through. Add pasta water as needed to make the sauce silky.

steps.raw_text: To serve, ladle the creamy macaroni into bowls and top with the crispy garlic breadcrumbs and the spring onion greens. Enjoy! (NB: If saving some for leftovers, heat it with a splash of vegan milk, reserved pasta water or water, as the pasta will absorb a lot of the sauce as it sits)
steps.label: Plate and garnish macaroni
steps.notes: Top with crispy breadcrumbs and spring onion greens. Leftovers can be reheated with milk or water.

title: Creamy Lemon Mafaldine Pasta, Refreshing Crunchy Sugarsnaps, Garden Peas, Peppery Rocket Salad & Chilli Pine Nut Crumb

steps.label: Prep vegetables and zest lemon
steps.notes: Zest and halve the lemon, trim the sugarsnaps, and finely slice the chilli.

steps.label: Toast pine nuts and chilli
steps.notes: Toast the pine nuts and sliced chilli in a dry pan until golden, then set aside as a crumb.

steps.label: Boil mafaldine pasta
steps.notes: Cook the mafaldine pasta in boiling salted water for 9-11 minutes until al dente, then drain.

steps.label: Sauté greens and make sauce
steps.notes: Sauté the sugarsnaps and garden peas, then stir in cream and lemon zest to simmer gently.

steps.label: Toss pasta in creamy sauce
steps.notes: Combine the drained mafaldine pasta with the creamy lemon and vegetable sauce, tossing to coat.

steps.label: Plate and garnish pasta
steps.notes: Divide the pasta among plates, top with fresh peppery rocket salad, and sprinkle with the chilli pine nut crumb.

title: Creamy Mattar Makhani with Tofu 'Paneer', Zingy Kachumbar Salad & Soft Garlic Naan

steps.raw_text: Tofu and peas are gently simmered in coconut milk and tomatoes with onion, garlic, turmeric and cardamom
steps.label: Simmer tofu and peas in curry sauce
steps.notes: Gently simmer the tofu and peas with the aromatics, coconut milk, and tomatoes to build the curry base.

steps.raw_text: zingy chopped salad made from red onion, cherry tomatoes, coriander and lime
steps.label: Prepare kachumbar salad
steps.notes: Chop the red onion, cherry tomatoes, and coriander, then dress with lime juice.

steps.raw_text: served alongside a zingy chopped salad... Served with a pillowy soft garlic and herb naan
steps.label: Plate and serve curry with salad and naan
steps.notes: Serve the warm mattar makhani curry alongside the fresh kachumbar salad and garlic & herb naan.

title: Creamy Orzo Al Limone With Crispy Panko Tofu, Roasted Cherry Tomatoes & Tenderstem Broccoli

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan, boil your kettle, and take out a roasting tray, a large saucepan and a frying pan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and boil kettle
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and boil the kettle.

steps.raw_text: Fill a saucepan with boiling water and place it over medium heat. Once boiling, add the orzo and cook for 9 minutes, or until al dente. Scoop out a cup of the pasta water for later, then drain the orzo and set it aside.
steps.label: Cook and drain the orzo
steps.notes: Cook for 9 minutes or until al dente. Remember to reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

steps.raw_text: Place the cherry tomatoes and tenderstem broccoli on a baking tray, and drizzle with some good-quality olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then roast for 10–15 minutes, until the tomatoes begin to burst and the tenderstem broccoli is lightly charred.
steps.label: Roast tomatoes and tenderstem broccoli
steps.notes: Roast for 10–15 minutes until tomatoes begin to burst and broccoli is lightly charred.

steps.raw_text: Take out two large bowls. Place the dry mix into a bowl and measure out 50ml (100ml for a 4-person portion) of plant milk (or water if you don’t have milk). Slowly add the milk or water and stir until you have a thick batter. Season well with salt and pepper and stir thoroughly until combined. Pour the panko into the other bowl and season with salt and pepper. Cut the tofu in half lengthwise, then in half again so you have four thin 'steak' like slices. Pat dry each piece with a sheet of kitchen towel and coat them in the batter, then toss it in the panko. Press gently to ensure the panko evenly covers all sides.
steps.label: Slice, batter, and bread tofu
steps.notes: Slice tofu into four thin steaks, pat dry, coat in batter, and press into panko.

steps.raw_text: Add about 1 cm of neutral oil to a frying pan and place it over medium-low heat. You can just add a drizzle of oil if you prefer but the tofu won't get quite as crispy. Once the oil is hot enough to sizzle when a small amount of panko is added, carefully place the coated tofu in the pan to fry. Turn the tofu as each side becomes crispy, cooking until all sides are golden, around 5 minutes total. Remove from the pan and place on kitchen paper to drain any excess oil.
steps.label: Fry the coated tofu steaks
steps.notes: Fry for around 5 minutes total until all sides are golden and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.

steps.raw_text: Place the saucepan you used for the orzo over a medium heat, add the creamy lemon sauce and gently warm through for a few minutes. Add the cooked orzo and stir well, then add a little of the reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce to your preferred consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Warm sauce and mix with orzo
steps.notes: Gently warm the sauce for a few minutes, stir in the orzo, and loosen with reserved pasta water.

title: Creamy Panang Curry With Tofu, Red Pepper, Baby Spinach, Sticky Jasmine Rice, Crushed Peanuts & Lime

steps.raw_text: Pre-heat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, then take out a baking tray, small saucepan and a deep frying pan or wok.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan and gather all necessary pans.

steps.raw_text: Tear the tofu into bitesized chunks, place into your roasting tray, toss through a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway. The tofu should be starting to turn brown and crispy on the outside.
steps.label: Prep and roast tofu
steps.notes: Roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until brown and crispy on the outside.

steps.raw_text: Place the jasmine rice into your small saucepan, cover with 1.25–1.5x its volume in water and place over a medium-high heat. Bring to the boil, stir then reduce to low and cover with a lid. Cook until tender and fluffy, around 8-10 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave to steam, covered, until ready to serve.
steps.label: Cook jasmine rice
steps.notes: Cook for 8-10 minutes (midpoint 9 used), then turn off heat and leave covered to steam.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan or wok over a medium heat and dry fry (without oil) the peanuts to toast. Remove and set aside. Lightly crush or chop the peanuts and wipe the pan clean with some kitchen towel.
steps.label: Toast and crush peanuts
steps.notes: Dry fry peanuts without oil, then wipe the pan clean for the next step.

steps.raw_text: Remove the stem and core from the red pepper and then finely slice. You could also slice some of the red pepper very finely and set aside as a garnish (optional).
