steps.raw_text: Place your cast iron griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of oil to coat the bottom. Once the pan is searing hot, add the marinaded mushroom skewers . We recommend compressing the oyster mushrooms with a spatula or slotted turner so that they flatten and get crispier. Cook until crispy and blackened a little, around 5 minutes on each side.
steps.label: Cook the mushroom skewers
steps.notes: Cook for around 5 minutes on each side until crispy and blackened. Compress with a spatula to flatten.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, drain and dice the cooked beetroot into 1.5-2cm cubes and place in a mixing bowl. Add the lemon yoghurt and season generously with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Prepare the beetroot raita
steps.notes: Dice beetroot into 1.5-2cm cubes and mix with lemon yoghurt in a bowl.

steps.raw_text: Divide the cooked basmati rice between serving bowls and ladle over the sri lankan daal . Top with the crispy spiced oyster mushroom skewer , garnish with a few picked coriander leaves , and serve with a side of beetroot raita . Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve the dish
steps.notes: Assemble bowls with rice, daal, skewers, coriander garnish, and a side of raita.

title: Crispy Black Pepper Tofu With Stir Fried Vegetables, Sticky Coconut Rice, Pak Choi & Sesame Seeds

steps.raw_text: Take out a saucepan and a wok (recommended) or large frying pan.
steps.label: Gather saucepan and wok or frying pan
steps.notes: Prepare cooking vessels before starting.

steps.raw_text: Place the rice in your saucepan and cover with 2.5x its volume in water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and cover. Allow to cook for 5 minutes, then stir through the desiccated coconut and continue cooking for a further 3-5 minutes or until tender but al dente.
steps.label: Cook coconut rice in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook rice for 5 minutes, then stir in coconut and cook for 3-5 minutes more until tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: Tear the tofu into bitesized pieces with your hands, then place into a bowl and toss through the cornflour until evenly coated. Add a drizzle of a neutral oil (e.g. vegetable, sunflower or groundnut, but not olive oil) to your frying pan or wok and once hot, add the tofu and fry until golden and crunchy on all sides, around 10 minutes. Transfer to a bowl lined with kitchen towel.
steps.label: Prep and fry the tofu
steps.notes: Tear tofu, coat in cornflour, and fry for around 10 minutes until golden and crunchy.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, deseed the red pepper and cut it into bite-sized pieces. Peel the onion , trim the top and base, and cut it into bite-sized pieces as well.
steps.label: Prep red pepper and onion
steps.notes: Deseed and chop pepper and onion into bite-sized pieces while other components cook.

steps.raw_text: Wipe the pan clean with a kitchen towel, then place it back on a medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, add the prepared red pepper and onion , and stir-fry until softened and lightly browned. Add the black pepper sauce and cook until simmering, about 2–3 minutes. Once the sauce is hot, return the tofu to the pan and stir through for 1–2 minutes, then remove from the heat.
steps.label: Stir-fry vegetables and combine with tofu
steps.notes: Simmer sauce for 2-3 minutes, then stir tofu through for 1-2 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Finely slice the spring onions . Slice the base off the pak choi stem and pull apart the leaves with your hands. Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, fry the pak choi until tender, around 3-5 minutes. Season to taste with soy or salt.
steps.label: Prep and fry the pak choi
steps.notes: Fry pak choi for 3-5 minutes until tender. Slice spring onions for garnish.

steps.raw_text: Serve the black pepper tofu alongside the coconut rice and charred pak choi . Scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds to garnish and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the dish
steps.notes: Garnish with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.

title: Crispy Cauliflower Baos Drenched In Tangy Five Spice Sauce With Tart Pickled Carrot & Daikon & Fresh Coriander
Crispy Chilli Tofu Tossed in Spring Onions & Sesame Seeds, With Sticky Jasmine Rice & Seasonal Greens

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a saucepan, a steamer (or a second saucepan if you don't have a steamer) and a deep frying pan or wok.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather all necessary pans and steamers before starting.

steps.raw_text: Add the jasmine rice to one of your saucepans and cover with 1.5x its volume of water. Place over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 8–10 minutes, or until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from the heat and leave to stand, covered, to steam before fluffing with a fork.
steps.label: Cook the jasmine rice
steps.notes: Cook covered for 8–10 minutes after boiling, then let stand covered to steam before fluffing.

steps.raw_text: Set your steamer over the hob and steam the kale for 5-10 minutes or until tender. If you don't have a steamer, you can boil the kale in water for the same time.
steps.label: Steam the kale
steps.notes: Steam for 5–10 minutes until tender. Alternatively, boil in water for the same duration.

steps.raw_text: Tear the tofu into bitesized pieces with your hands, then place into a bowl and toss through the cornflour mix until evenly coated. Add a drizzle of a neutral oil (e.g. vegetable, sunflower, groundnut) to your frying pan or wok and once hot, add the tofu and fry until golden and crispy on all sides, then transfer to a bowl lined with kitchen towel. Meanwhile, remove the stem and core from the red pepper and cut into 0.5cm thick slices. Finely slice the spring onions and separate the white part and green part.
steps.label: Prep and fry tofu, slice veg
steps.notes: Tear and coat tofu, then fry until golden. Meanwhile, slice the red pepper and spring onions.

steps.raw_text: Drain any excess oil from the frying pan, then add the sliced red pepper and the white parts of the spring onions . Cook over medium-high heat until tender but still al dente (about 3–5 minutes). Add the chilli sauce , stir through, and cook until it thickens to a sticky consistency. You may add a splash of water if it reduces too much. Once the sauce is hot, return the crispy tofu to the pan, stir for 1–2 minutes to make sure all the pieces are coated in the sauce.
steps.label: Cook veg and toss tofu in sauce
steps.notes: Cook peppers and white spring onions for 3–5 minutes, thicken the sauce, then toss tofu for 1–2 minutes.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the jasmine rice , chilli tofu and steamed kale between serving bowls. Scatter over the green part of the sliced spring onions and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish
steps.notes: Divide rice, tofu, and kale into bowls, then scatter the green spring onions on top.

title: Slow-Cooked Moroccan Stew With Sticky Dates, Green Olives & A Zesty Chermoula Dressing
Sticky Sesame Ginger Tofu Rice Bowl With Kimchi Mayo, Pickled Cabbage, Carrot, Edamame & Sesame Seeds

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a large frying pan and a saucepan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set out the required pans.

steps.raw_text: Fill the saucepan with the boiling water from your kettle and place it over medium heat. Blanch the edamame for 1–2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
steps.label: Blanch the edamame
steps.notes: Blanch the edamame in boiling water for 1–2 minutes, then drain and set aside.

steps.raw_text: Rinse the sushi rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well. Add to a saucepan with 1.25–1.5x its volume of cold water and, if you have time, leave to soak for 10–15 minutes. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 10 minutes without lifting the lid. Turn off the heat and leave to steam, covered, until ready to serve.
steps.label: Rinse, soak, and cook sushi rice
steps.notes: Includes optional 10–15 minute soak, 10 minutes cooking covered on low heat, and steaming time.

steps.raw_text: Finely slice the spring onions and separate the green and white parts.
steps.label: Slice the spring onions
steps.notes: Finely slice and separate the green and white parts.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of neutral oil. Tear the tofu into bite-sized chunks with your hands, and add them to the frying pan once the oil is hot. Fry until golden and crispy on all sides, about 10 minutes. Add the white part of the spring onions and the sticky sesame dressing , stir to coat the tofu evenly, and cook for a further 2–3 minutes until the sauce is slightly thickened.
steps.label: Fry tofu and add dressing
steps.notes: Fry torn tofu for 10 minutes until golden, then add white spring onions and dressing for 2–3 minutes.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, julienne the carrot . Alternatively, you can use a vegetable peeler to make thick ribbons or grate it using a coarse grater. Combine it with the rice vinegar pickled red cabbage in a mixing bowl and let it marinate.
steps.label: Prepare and marinate carrot and cabbage
steps.notes: Julienne, peel, or grate the carrot, then combine with pickled red cabbage to marinate.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the sushi rice , sticky sesame ginger tofu , and the marinated carrot and red cabbage mixture between serving bowls. Drizzle with the kimchi mayo and finish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and the green parts of the spring onions . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish bowls
steps.notes: Divide rice, tofu, and marinated vegetables. Garnish with kimchi mayo, sesame seeds, and green spring onions.

title: Sticky Teriyaki Tofu Bowl With Purple Sprouting Broccoli & Pickled Cabbage Over Sushi Rice

steps.raw_text: Take out two frying pans and a saucepan. Shake the teriyaki sauce pouch well before using, in case any of the cornflour has separated from the dressing while chilled.
steps.label: Prepare pans and shake teriyaki sauce
steps.notes: Shake the teriyaki sauce pouch well to recombine any separated cornflour.

steps.raw_text: Rinse the sushi rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well. Add to a saucepan with 1.25~1.5x its volume of cold water and, if you have time, leave to soak for 10–15 minutes. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 10 minutes without lifting the lid. Turn off the heat and leave to steam, covered, until ready to serve.
steps.label: Rinse, soak, and cook sushi rice
steps.notes: Includes optional 10-15 minute soak, 10 minutes of active cooking on low heat, and steaming time.

steps.raw_text: Tear the tofu into bite-sized chunks with your hands and heat a drizzle of oil in each of your two frying pans over a medium heat.
steps.label: Tear tofu and heat oil in pans
steps.notes: Tear tofu into bite-sized chunks by hand. Heat oil over medium heat.

steps.raw_text: Add the tofu to one of your frying pans and fry until golden and crispy on all sides, around 10 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside. Add the teriyaki sauce to the pan and cook until the sauce has thickened a little (1-2 minutes), then take the pan off the heat, add the crispy tofu back into the pan and stir it through the sauce until well coated.
steps.label: Fry tofu and coat in teriyaki sauce
steps.notes: Fry tofu for around 10 minutes until golden and crispy. Cook sauce for 1-2 minutes to thicken before tossing tofu back in.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile add the broccoli to your other pan and fry on all sides until tender but al dente. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Finely slice the spring onion while everything cooks. You can chop the broccoli up into bite-sized pieces before serving if you prefer.
steps.label: Fry broccoli and slice spring onion
steps.notes: Fry broccoli until tender but al dente. Finely slice spring onion while everything cooks.

steps.raw_text: Divide the sushi rice , sautéed broccoli and pickled cabbage between serving bowls. Top with the teriyaki tofu , spoon over any extra sauce, then sprinkle over the sliced spring onion and sesame seeds to garnish. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble bowls and garnish
steps.notes: Divide rice, broccoli, and pickled cabbage. Top with teriyaki tofu, extra sauce, sliced spring onion, and sesame seeds.

title: Summer Coconut & Turmeric Daal With Tangy Courgette Pickle, Crispy Kale & Red Quinoa

steps.raw_text: Tender red lentils and sweet potatoes are gently simmered in coconut milk with cumin, turmeric, mustard seeds, garlic and ginger.
steps.label: Simmer coconut & turmeric daal
steps.notes: Gently simmer the lentils and sweet potatoes in the spiced coconut milk until tender.

steps.raw_text: fluffy red quinoa
steps.label: Cook red quinoa
steps.notes: Cook the red quinoa until fluffy.

steps.raw_text: crispy cavolo nero
steps.label: Crisp cavolo nero
steps.notes: Prepare and crisp the cavolo nero (kale).

steps.raw_text: tangy turmeric-spiked courgette pickle
steps.label: Prepare courgette pickle
steps.notes: Combine courgette with turmeric and pickling ingredients.

steps.raw_text: Served with a tangy turmeric-spiked courgette pickle, crispy cavolo nero and fluffy red quinoa.
steps.label: Assemble and serve
steps.notes: Plate the daal alongside the fluffy quinoa, crispy cavolo nero, and tangy courgette pickle.

title: Sun Dried Tomato Lasagne Soup With Spinach, Cannellini Beans & Cheesy Cashew Cream
Super Green Cheats Lasagne With Courgette, Butter Beans, Miso Bechamel, Toasted Nuts & Seeds

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a large casserole dish or an oven-proof deep pan, along with a blender or a large mixing bowl and a stick blender. Don't worry if you don't have a blender as we will provide an alternative method below.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan). Get out the casserole dish and blending equipment.

steps.raw_text: Place your casserole dish or ovenproof pan over medium-high heat and drizzle in some olive oil. Slice the courgette into 0.5cm rounds, add to the pan, and sauté until they are softened and lightly browned.
steps.label: Slice and sauté courgette
steps.notes: Slice courgette into 0.5cm rounds and sauté over medium-high heat until softened and lightly browned.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, add the super green lasagne sauce and baby spinach into a blender, and blend until the sauce is smooth and vibrant green. Alternatively, you can use a mixing bowl and a stick blender for this process. We deliver the sauce and spinach separately for better flavour and colour. If you don't have a blender, you can alternatively wilt the spinach in the sauce by gently heating in a small saucepan for a few minutes. Once the courgettes have softened a little, pour the sauce into the pan along with 50ml of water (double the measurement for a four person portion size), and the butter beans (including the water). Give everything a good mix and cook until it's lightly bubbling, around 3 minutes.
steps.label: Blend sauce and simmer with beans
steps.notes: Blend spinach and sauce. Once courgettes are softened, add sauce, 50ml water, and butter beans. Simmer for around 3 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Break the lasagne sheets into 3-4 pieces each and add them to the simmering super green lasagne sauce , a few sheets at a time, stir well to ensure the lasagne sheets are separated and evenly distributed in the sauce, then place the dish in the pre-heated oven and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the lasagne from the oven, pour over the miso bechamel and return it to the oven for another 15-20 minutes or until the bechamel is a little thicker. If you have time, leave the lasagne to rest for 5 minutes before serving so it’s easier to cut and serve.
steps.label: Assemble and bake lasagne
steps.notes: Bake for 10 minutes, add miso bechamel, bake for another 15-20 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, toast the nuts & seeds by dry frying (without oil) in a small frying pan until golden, around 2-4 minutes.
steps.label: Toast nuts and seeds
steps.notes: Dry fry in a small pan without oil for 2-4 minutes until golden.

steps.raw_text: To serve, drizzle or scatter the toasted nuts & seeds over the wild garlic lasagne , divide between serving bowls and enjoy!
steps.label: Garnish and serve lasagne
steps.notes: Scatter toasted nuts and seeds over the lasagne and divide into bowls.

title: Super Green Gnocchi With Creamy Spinach & Kale Sauce, Garden Peas, Vegan Burrata & Chilli Pine Nut Crumb
Super Green Grain Bowl With Roasted Squash, Crispy Chickpeas,  Creamy Garlic Tahini & Pomegranate Seeds

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan. Boil your kettle and take out two baking trays and a saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and boil kettle
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan).

steps.raw_text: Add the boiling water from the kettle to your saucepan, lightly salt it, and bring back to the boil over a medium heat. Add the farro and cook until tender, about 15–20 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.label: Cook farro in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook farro for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain and set aside.

steps.raw_text: Halve the butternut squash and remove the seeds using a spoon. Cut each half into wedges about 2cm thick. Place on one of the baking trays, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes, or until the edges start to caramelise.
steps.label: Prep and roast butternut squash
steps.notes: Roast for 20 minutes or until edges start to caramelize.

steps.raw_text: Drain and rinse the chickpeas , then divide them in half. Toss one half with a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Spread onto the second baking tray and add to the oven when the butternut squash has 10 minutes of cooking time remaining.
steps.label: Prep and roast chickpeas
steps.notes: Add chickpeas to the oven when the butternut squash has 10 minutes of cooking time remaining.

steps.raw_text: Once the farro is cooked, add it to a mixing bowl along with the reserved half of the chickpeas from STEP 4. Pour over the herby zhoug dressing and mix well. Add the baby spinach and toss to combine. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
steps.label: Mix farro salad
steps.notes: Combine cooked farro, reserved raw chickpeas, zhoug dressing, and baby spinach.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the super green farro , chickpeas , and baby spinach between serving bowls. Top with the roasted butternut squash wedges and crispy chickpeas . Finish with a drizzle of garlic tahini sauce and scatter over the pomegranate seeds . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve bowls
steps.notes: Top farro mixture with roasted squash, crispy chickpeas, garlic tahini, and pomegranate seeds.

title: Super Green Noodle Soup With Mangetout, Baby Sweetcorn, Oyster Mushrooms & Gochugaru Sesame Sprinkle
Super Green Saag Daal With Crispy Curry Spiced Tofu, Coconut Yoghurt, Pink Pickled Onion & Basmati Rice

steps.raw_text: Take out a small saucepan, a large saucepan and a large frying pan.
steps.label: Gather pans and saucepans
steps.notes: Gather all necessary cookware before starting.

steps.raw_text: Place the basmati rice into one of your saucepans and cover with 1.5x its volume in water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from the heat and leave to steam with the lid on until the rest of the dish is ready.
steps.label: Cook the basmati rice
steps.notes: Simmer for 10-12 minutes until water is absorbed, then leave to steam with the lid on.

steps.raw_text: Add the saag daal sauce to a large saucepan along with 200ml of water, then place over medium heat. Stir in the red lentils and bring to a boil. Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 15–20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender. Add a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick or starts to stick to the bottom. When the daal is almost ready, add the baby spinach to a blender with 100ml of water (double the amount for a four-person portion) and blend until smooth and vibrant green. Alternatively, you can use a mixing bowl with a stick blender. Stir the green sauce through the daal and cook for 1-2 minutes. If you don't have a blender, you can finely chop the spinach instead and stir it into the daal to wilt. We deliver the spinach and sauce separately and add at the end of cooking to keep the super green colour, but wilting it is just as delicious! Season with salt and pepper to taste.
steps.label: Cook the saag daal
steps.notes: Simmer lentils for 15-20 minutes. Blend spinach with 100ml water and stir in for the final 1-2 minutes. Alternatively, finely chop spinach if no blender is available.

steps.raw_text: Cut the tofu into bite-sized cubes, about 1.5 - 2cm in size. Place your frying pan over a medium-high heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the tofu to the pan and fry until golden all over. Sprinkle in the tofu spice mix and cook for a few more minutes or until the spice mix has cooked off a little and the tofu is golden brown. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Prep and fry tofu
steps.notes: Cut tofu into 1.5-2cm cubes. Fry until golden, then add spice mix and cook for a few more minutes.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the cooked basmati rice between serving bowls and spoon over the super green saag daal . Top with the crispy curry spiced tofu cubes, then garnish with the red wine vinegar pickled red onion and a dollop of coconut yoghurt . Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish
steps.notes: Assemble bowls with rice, daal, tofu, pickled red onion, and coconut yoghurt.

title: Super Green Spinach Gnocchi With Asparagus, 'Burrata' & Toasted Hazelnuts
Super Green Spring Minestrone With Asparagus, Regenerative Spelt Conchiglietti, & Wild Garlic Pesto

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle. Take out a small saucepan for the pasta and a deep frying pan, or a large, wide saucepan, to make the minestrone in.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
equipment: deep frying pan or large wide saucepan
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set out the required pans.

steps.raw_text: Fill your small saucepan with boiling water from the kettle, place it over medium heat, and bring it back to a boil. Once boiling, add a generous amount of salt, followed by the spelt conchiglietti pasta. Cook until al dente, about 10–12 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.label: Cook spelt conchiglietti pasta
steps.notes: Cook pasta for 10-12 minutes until al dente, then drain and set aside.

steps.raw_text: Remove the woody ends of the asparagus spears and slice them into bite-sized pieces. Place your larger pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the sliced asparagus and sauté for 5 minutes, or until tender but still al dente. Remove from the pan and set aside. STEP 3 Using the same pan over medium heat, add the spring minestrone with 200 ml of water (double the volume for the 4 person portion) and the drained butter beans . Simmer for 3–4 minutes to soften the beans slightly, then add the peas and baby spinach. Cook for a further 2–3 minutes, until the spinach has wilted. Add the cooked conchiglietti pasta and asparagus , then remove from the heat. Stir through half of the wild garlic pesto and season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Sauté asparagus and cook minestrone
equipment: deep frying pan or large wide saucepan
steps.notes: Sauté asparagus for 5 minutes. Simmer beans for 3-4 minutes, then cook peas and spinach for 2-3 minutes. Combine with cooked pasta at the end.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the minestrone between bowls and finish with a drizzle of the remaining wild garlic pesto and some finely sliced red chilli for a little kick. Enjoy!
steps.label: Garnish and serve minestrone
steps.notes: Divide into bowls, drizzle with remaining pesto, and garnish with finely sliced red chilli.

title: Super Green Minestrone With Basil Pesto, Orecchiette, Peas, Leeks, Courgette & Cannellini Beans

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a small saucepan for the orecchiette pasta and a deep frying pan, or large and wide saucepan to make the minestrone in. Slice the courgette into thin rounds. This is all your prep done.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prep ingredients
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and slice the courgette into thin rounds to complete all prep.

steps.raw_text: Fill your small saucepan with boiling water from the kettle, place it over medium heat, and bring it back to a boil. Once boiling, add a generous amount of salt, then add the orecchiette . Cook until al dente, about 10-13 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.label: Cook orecchiette pasta until al dente
steps.notes: Cook pasta in salted boiling water for 10-13 minutes (midpoint 11.5 minutes) until al dente, then drain.

steps.raw_text: Place your larger pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the sliced courgette and fry for 5 minutes or until tender, but al dente. Add the spring minestrone with 200ml of water and the drained cannellini beans . Simmer for 3-4 minutes to soften the beans a little, then add the peas and baby spinach and cook for a further 2-3 minutes until the spinach has wilted. Add the cooked orecchiette and remove from the heat. Stir through half of the basil pesto then season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Cook vegetables and combine with pasta
steps.notes: Fry courgettes for 5 minutes, simmer beans for 3-4 minutes, and cook greens for 2-3 minutes before stirring in the cooked pasta and half the pesto.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the minestrone soup between serving bowls and finish with a drizzle of the remaining basil pesto and some finely sliced red chilli for a little kick. Enjoy!
steps.label: Portion soup and garnish to serve
steps.notes: Divide soup into bowls, drizzle with remaining pesto, and top with finely sliced red chilli.

title: Super Green Spring Orzo With Peas, Asparagus, Spinach, Creamy Cashew 'Labneh' & Toasted Almonds

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a large saucepan and a frying pan
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set out the required pans.

steps.raw_text: Fill your saucepan with boiling water and place over a medium heat. Once boiling, add the orzo and cook for 6-8 minutes or until al dente. Scoop out a cup of the pasta water and save it.
steps.label: Cook orzo in saucepan
steps.notes: Cook the orzo for 6-8 minutes (midpoint 7) until al dente. Remember to scoop out and save a cup of pasta water before draining.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and dry fry (without oil) the al monds to toast. Remove from the pan, set aside and wipe the pan clean. When there's 5 minutes left on the orzo, place the frying pan back over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the asparagus and fry until charred a little on all sides and tender but al dente in the centre. Season well with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Toast almonds and fry asparagus
steps.notes: Dry fry almonds first, then wipe pan. When 5 minutes remain on the orzo, fry the asparagus in oil until lightly charred and tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: Drain the orzo and return it to the pan with the creamy green sauce , peas and spinach and place back over the heat. Cook until the spinach is wilted and the sauce is piping hot. Add a splash of your reserved pasta water to loosen it up if needed.
steps.label: Mix orzo with sauce and greens
steps.notes: Drain the orzo, return to the pan, and cook with sauce, peas, and spinach until spinach is wilted and sauce is piping hot. Loosen with pasta water if needed.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spoon the orzo into bowls, top with the asparagus and a dollop of creamy cashew labneh . Drizzle over some olive oil, sprinkle over the almonds and season to taste with sea salt and black pepper. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish orzo
steps.notes: Spoon orzo into bowls, top with asparagus, cashew labneh, olive oil, toasted almonds, and seasoning.

title: Super Green Orzotto With Peas, Tenderstem Broccoli, Spinach, Creamy Cashew 'Labneh' & Toasted Almonds

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a large saucepan and a frying pan
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set out the required pans to prepare for cooking.

steps.raw_text: Fill your saucepan with boiling water and place over a medium heat. Once boiling, add the orzo and cook for 6-8 minutes or until al dente. Scoop out a cup of the pasta water and save it.
steps.label: Cook orzo and save water
steps.notes: Cook the orzo for 6-8 minutes until al dente. Remember to scoop out and reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and dry fry (without oil) the flaked almonds to toast. Remove from the pan, set aside and wipe the pan clean. When there's 5 minutes left on the orzo, place the frying pan back over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the tenderstem broccoli and fry until charred a little on all sides and tender but al dente in the centre. Season well with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Toast almonds and fry broccoli
steps.notes: Dry fry almonds first, then set aside. Start frying the broccoli when there are 5 minutes left on the orzo timer.

steps.raw_text: Drain the orzo and return it to the pan with the creamy green sauce , peas and spinach and place back over the heat. Cook until the spinach is wilted and the sauce is piping hot. Add a splash of your reserved pasta water to loosen it up if needed.
steps.label: Combine orzo, sauce, and greens
steps.notes: Drain the orzo, return to the pan, and cook with the sauce, peas, and spinach until wilted and hot. Loosen with pasta water if needed.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spoon the orzo into bowls, top with the tenderstem broccoli and a dollop of creamy cashew labneh . Drizzle over some olive oil, sprinkle over the almonds and season to taste with sea salt and black pepper. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish orzotto
steps.notes: Spoon orzo into bowls, top with broccoli, cashew labneh, olive oil, toasted almonds, and seasoning.

title: Super Green Vegetable Garden Risotto With Garden Peas, Courgettes, Mint & Toasted Hazelnuts

steps.raw_text: Take out a frying pan and a saucepan. Pour boiling water from your kettle into a large saucepan, salt the water, then place over a medium-high heat.
steps.label: Heat water in saucepan
steps.notes: Pour boiling water from kettle into saucepan and heat over medium-high heat.

steps.raw_text: Once the water is bubbling, add the pearl barley and turn it down to a simmer. Cook until al dente, around 20 minutes. Reserve a mug of water for later, then drain the pearl barley once cooked. Meanwhile slice the courgette lengthways 0.5cm thick (or you could cut into cubes if you prefer!). Pick and finely chop the mint leaves.
steps.label: Simmer barley and prep veg
steps.notes: Simmer barley for around 20 minutes until al dente. Slice courgette and chop mint while it cooks.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat, then add the hazelnuts and dry fry (without oil) until golden, around 2-3 minutes. Remove, set aside and lightly crush or chop. When the pearl barley is almost ready, add a drizzle of oil to your frying pan and fry the courgette until lightly charred. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Toast hazelnuts and fry courgette
steps.notes: Dry fry hazelnuts for 2-3 minutes over medium heat, then fry courgettes when barley is almost ready.

steps.raw_text: Once the pearl barley is ready, put the empty saucepan back over a medium-low heat, add the super green sauce and g arden peas , and heat through until piping hot . Add the cooked pearl barley back into the pan along with half of the chopped mint (reserving the rest for the final garnish!) and squeeze in half of the lemon . Add a little of the reserved pearl barley water if needed so the sauce is nice and creamy. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Combine barley and green sauce
steps.notes: Heat sauce and peas over medium-low heat until piping hot, then stir in barley, half the mint, and lemon.

steps.raw_text: Divide the risotto between serving bowls, then top with the charred courgettes , a scattering of toasted hazelnuts , the remaining mint and another squeeze of fresh lemon . Season to taste with salt and pepper and finish with a good drizzle of extra virgin olive oil if you like. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish risotto
steps.notes: Top with charred courgettes, toasted hazelnuts, remaining mint, lemon, and optional olive oil.

title: Super Green Udon Noodles With Tenderstem Broccoli, Crispy Sesame Crusted Tofu & Rayu Chilli Drizzle

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a sauce pan and a large frying pan. Fill your saucepan with boiling water from your kettle, place over a high heat and bring to the boil for the noodles.
steps.label: Boil water in saucepan
steps.notes: Boil kettle first, then transfer water to saucepan on high heat to bring to a boil.

steps.raw_text: Add the udon noodles to your saucepan of boiling water and cook for 5–6 minutes, or until tender but still al dente. Once cooked, drain and rinse the noodles under cold water - this helps remove excess starch and prevents them from becoming soggy. Set them aside in a colander to drain.
steps.label: Cook and drain udon noodles
steps.notes: Cook noodles for 5-6 minutes until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.raw_text: Add the super green noodle sauce and baby spinach to a blender and blend until smooth and vibrant green. Alternatively, use a hand blender in a bowl, or finely chop the baby spinach and fold it into the sauce.
steps.label: Blend green sauce and spinach
steps.notes: Can use a standard blender, hand blender in a bowl, or finely chop spinach and fold in.

steps.raw_text: Cut the tenderstem broccoli into bite-sized pieces. Place your frying pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the tenderstem broccoli and fry for 4-5 minutes, until slightly charred and tender but still with a bit of bite. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
steps.label: Prep and fry broccoli
steps.notes: Cut broccoli into bite-sized pieces and fry for 4-5 minutes until slightly charred.

steps.raw_text: Dice the tofu into 1.5cm cubes. Take out two small bowls. Add the sesame seed mix and cornflour to one bowl and combine well. Fill the other bowl with water. Dip each tofu cube in the water, then roll it in the sesame seed and cornflour mixture to coat all sides. Repeat with the remaining tofu. In the same frying pan you used to cook the tenderstem broccoli, add another drizzle of oil. Once hot, fry the sesame-coated tofu cubes for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy on all sides. Remove from your pan and set aside on a plate. Alternatively, you can bake the sesame-crusted tofu. Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan. Arrange the coated tofu cubes in a single layer on a baking tray and spray generously with oil for the crispiest result. Bake for 20 minutes, turning halfway through cooking.
steps.label: Prep and cook sesame tofu
steps.notes: Dice and coat tofu. Fry for 6-8 minutes, or bake at 220°C (200°C fan) for 20 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Wipe your frying pan clean and place it back over medium heat. Add the super green sauce and warm through for 2-3 minutes, until lightly simmering. Once the sauce is piping hot, add the cooked udon noodles and tenderstem broccoli, then stir until well combined and heated through. STEP 6 To serve, divide the super green udon noodles between serving bowls and top with the crispy sesame crusted tofu . Drizzle with the smoky black bean rayu and enjoy!
steps.label: Combine, warm, and serve
steps.notes: Warm sauce for 2-3 minutes, toss with noodles and broccoli, top with tofu and rayu drizzle.

title: Super Green Wholewheat Rigatoni With Wild Garlic Sauce, Peas, Cavolo Nero, Creamy 'Burrata' & Chilli Pine Nut Crumb

steps.raw_text: Boil the kettle and take out two saucepans and a frying pan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather two saucepans and a frying pan.

steps.raw_text: Place one of your saucepans over medium heat and pour in the boiling water from the kettle, adding a pinch of salt. Remove the hard stems from the cavolo nero , tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces, and add half to the boiling water. Cook until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Set the remaining cavolo nero aside.
steps.label: Prep and wilt half the cavolo nero
steps.notes: Cook cavolo nero until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Set the remaining cavolo nero aside.

steps.raw_text: Using a slotted spoon, transfer the wilted cavolo nero to the second saucepan. Add the wholewheat rigatoni to the boiling water and cook for 11–13 minutes, until al dente.
steps.label: Boil rigatoni until al dente
steps.notes: Cook pasta for 11–13 minutes until al dente. Transfer wilted cavolo nero to the second saucepan.

steps.raw_text: Add the wild garlic & basil sauce to the pan with the wilted cavolo nero and blend with a hand blender until smooth. Alternatively, if you don’t have a blender, finely chop the cavolo nero and stir it through the sauce. Place the sauce over medium heat, add the garden peas , and cook until warmed through, about 5–6 minutes.
steps.label: Blend sauce and cook with peas
steps.notes: Blend sauce with wilted cavolo nero until smooth (or finely chop if no blender). Cook with peas for 5–6 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, place the frying pan over medium heat and add the pine nut crumb . Dry toast (without oil) for 1–2 minutes, until slightly golden and aromatic. Remove from the pan and set aside. Return the frying pan to medium-high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Sauté the remaining cavolo nero until crispy at the edges, about 4–5 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Toast pine nuts and sauté cavolo nero
steps.notes: Dry toast pine nuts for 1–2 minutes, then sauté remaining cavolo nero for 4–5 minutes until crispy at the edges.

steps.raw_text: Just before serving, add the cooked wholewheat rigatoni to the wild garlic & basil sauce and combine well. Divide between serving bowls and top with a dollop of cashew 'burrata' . Sprinkle over the pine nut crumb and serve the crispy cavolo nero on the side. Enjoy!
steps.label: Combine pasta with sauce and plate
steps.notes: Combine pasta and sauce, top with cashew burrata, pine nut crumb, and serve crispy cavolo nero on the side.

title: Superfood Black Bean Chilli Over Roasted Sweet Potato With Zingy Guacamole & Crunchy Tortilla Chips

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a baking tray and a saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare equipment
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan.

steps.raw_text: Prick the sweet potato all over with a paring knife or fork, then microwave on high for 5-6 minutes, rotating halfway through (be careful as they will be hot). Place onto a baking tray, cover in olive oil, salt and pepper and then roast in the oven for 15 minutes or until soft. If you don't have a microwave you can bake the sweet potato from raw but it will take longer - just slice in half (or quarters if it’s a very large potato) lengthways, rub with olive oil, salt and pepper, and cook cut-side up until lightly browned and tender, around 30 minutes depending on the size of the sweet potato.
steps.label: Prep and roast sweet potato
steps.notes: Microwave for 5-6 minutes, then roast for 15 minutes. If baking from raw without a microwave, it will take around 30 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Use scissors or a knife to cut the fresh corn tortillas into triangles, place into your smaller baking tray and drizzle or brush them with a little olive oil. Once the sweet potato has had 5 minutes, bake the corn tortillas for the final 10 minutes of cooking time until perfectly crispy, turning halfway through. Season with a little salt and pepper. Remove and set aside.
steps.label: Cut and bake tortilla chips
steps.notes: Bake for the final 10 minutes of the sweet potato's cooking time, turning halfway through.

steps.raw_text: Drain the black beans and reserve the juices. Add the superfood chilli sauce to your saucepan along with the black beans . When there's around 5 minutes left on the sweet potato, place over a medium-high heat and warm through until piping hot, around 5 minutes. If the sauce reduces too much, add a little of the reserved black bean juices while cooking.
steps.label: Warm the black bean chilli
steps.notes: Warm through for 5 minutes when there is 5 minutes left on the sweet potato. Add reserved bean juices if the sauce reduces too much.

steps.raw_text: To make the guacamole, scoop out the flesh from the avocado and place into a bowl. Finely chop the coriander (reserving a few leaves for garnishing) and add to the bowl with the avocado. Squeeze in the lime juice to taste, season with salt and add a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil (optional). Mash the avocado up with a fork and give everything a good stir to combine the flavours.
steps.label: Prepare the guacamole
steps.notes: Mash avocado with a fork and reserve a few coriander leaves for garnish.

steps.raw_text: Remove the sweet potato from the oven, slice open lengthways and place half on each serving bowl or plate. Serve the superfood chilli over the top and then garnish with guacamole and serve the tortilla chips alongside. Garnish with any remaining coriander and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the dish
steps.notes: Slice open the sweet potato, top with chilli, guacamole, tortilla chips, and remaining coriander.

title: Sweet Potato Shepherds Pie With Rich Mushroom Lentil Red Wine Ragu & Wilted Green Kale

steps.raw_text: Take out a saucepan, a hob-safe casserole dish, and a frying pan. If you would like to bake the top of the sweet potato mash layer, preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan.
steps.label: Prepare equipment and preheat oven
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan) if you plan to bake the sweet potato mash top.

steps.raw_text: Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2 cm cubes and add them to your saucepan along with enough water to cover. Place over medium-high heat, bring to a boil, and cook for 15 minutes, or until fork-tender. Once cooked, drain well and mash with a masher or the back of a fork until you reach your desired consistency. You may want to add a knob of plant-based butter or a splash of plant milk for extra creaminess. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Prep, boil, and mash sweet potatoes
steps.notes: Boil for 15 minutes or until fork-tender. Mash with optional plant-based butter or milk for creaminess.

steps.raw_text: To prepare the ragu, add a drizzle of olive oil to your casserole dish and place over medium heat. Finely chop the chestnut mushrooms , add them to the casserole dish, and cook for 5–6 minutes, or until the mushrooms are tender and browned off. Drain the black lentils and add them to the mushrooms along with the ragu sauce . Stir well, bring to a simmer, and cook for a further 5 minutes. Once the ragu is ready, season with salt and pepper, turn off the heat, and layer the sweet potato mash on top. It is ready to serve as it is, but if you would like a crispy top, place the dish under the grill for 5-10 minutes.
steps.label: Cook ragu and assemble pie
steps.notes: Cook mushrooms for 5–6 minutes, simmer ragu for 5 minutes, and optionally grill the assembled pie for 5–10 minutes (midpoint used for timing).

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, place your frying pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Remove the hardy stems from the curly kale and tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add to the pan along with a splash of water and cook until wilted and vibrant green, about 5–6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Sauté the curly kale
steps.notes: Cook kale for 5–6 minutes until wilted and vibrant green.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the shepherd’s pie between serving bowls with a side of wilted curly kale . Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve shepherd's pie
steps.notes: Divide the shepherd's pie and wilted kale into serving bowls.

title: Sweet & Spicy Jerk Tofu Over Fluffy Coconut Rice, With Mango, Avocado & Cucumber Salad

steps.raw_text: Take out a saucepan, a mixing bowl and a large frying pan.
steps.label: Gather cooking equipment
steps.notes: Retrieve the saucepan, mixing bowl, and large frying pan to prepare for cooking.

steps.raw_text: Add the basmati rice to your saucepan and cover with 2x its volume in water and stir in the desiccated coconut . Place over medium-high heat and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover with a lid and cook until fluffy, around 8 minutes.
steps.label: Cook the coconut rice
steps.notes: Bring to a boil on medium-high, then cover and cook on low for around 8 minutes until fluffy.

steps.raw_text: Roughly chop the coriander and cut the mango and avocado into small, bite-sized pieces. Add them to your mixing bowl along with the lime pickled cucumber , then drizzle in some of the pickle liquid from the bag to dress the salad. Toss everything together, season with salt and pepper to taste, and set aside.
steps.label: Prepare mango avocado salad
steps.notes: Chop coriander, mango, and avocado. Toss with pickled cucumber and pickle liquid in the mixing bowl.

steps.raw_text: Tear the tofu into bite-sized chunks with your hands. Heat a drizzle of oil in your flying pan over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 5-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy on all sides. Remove the tofu from the pan and turn the heat down to low-medium. Add the jerk sauce and warm through for 30-60 seconds. Take the pan off the heat (to keep the tofu crispy), then add the the tofu back into the pan. Stir gently until the tofu is all evenly coated.
steps.label: Fry and sauce tofu
steps.notes: Fry tofu for 5-10 minutes until crispy. Warm sauce for 30-60 seconds, then coat tofu off the heat.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the coconut rice , mango , avocado , and cucumber salad , along with the jerk tofu and any remaining sauce from the pan, between serving bowls. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and serve
steps.notes: Divide the coconut rice, salad, and jerk tofu into serving bowls and enjoy.

title: Tahini Miso Ramen With Crispy Chilli Tempeh, Pak Choi & Flat Rice Noodles

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a large frying pan and two saucepans.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather one large frying pan and two saucepans.

steps.raw_text: Crumble the tempeh with your hands until minced. Remove the pak choi leaves from the base of the stem using your hands. Finely dice the chilli and spring onions (including the green bits!).
steps.label: Prep tempeh, pak choi, and aromatics
steps.notes: Crumble the tempeh by hand, remove pak choi leaves from the stem base, and finely dice the chilli and spring onions.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over high heat and add a generous drizzle of oil. Add the crumbled tempeh to your frying pan and fry until crispy, around 5 minutes. Stir through half of the black bean rayu , then remove from the pan and keep warm.
steps.label: Fry crumbled tempeh until crispy
steps.notes: Fry over high heat for around 5 minutes until crispy, stir in half of the black bean rayu, then remove and keep warm.

steps.raw_text: Pour boiling water from your kettle into your first saucepan and place over a medium-high heat. Once the water is bubbling, add the flat rice noodles and cook for 4-5 minutes or until tender but al dente. Keep checking as rice noodles can be easily overcooked. Drain and rinse well under cold running water, then leave them in a colander to drain.
steps.label: Cook and drain rice noodles
steps.notes: Cook in bubbling water for 4-5 minutes until tender but al dente. Drain and rinse under cold running water to prevent overcooking.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, pour the miso tahini broth into your other saucepan and add 300ml of water (double the measurement for a four person portion size). Place it over medium-high heat and bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat to a light simmer until ready to serve.
steps.label: Boil and simmer miso tahini broth
steps.notes: Bring broth and 300ml water (double for 4 people) to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a light simmer until ready to serve.

steps.raw_text: Wipe clean the same frying pan you used to cook the tempeh with kitchen towel, then add the pak choi and cook until tender, around 5 minutes (you can do this step while you serve up the rest of the ramen as below).
steps.label: Cook pak choi in frying pan
steps.notes: Wipe the pan clean with a kitchen towel first. Cook pak choi for around 5 minutes until tender. This can run in parallel with serving up.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the noodles between serving bowls, pour over the hot miso tahini broth , then top with the pak choi and chilli tempeh . Garnish with chilli , spring onions and a drizzle of the remaining black bean rayu . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish ramen bowls
steps.notes: Divide noodles, pour hot broth, top with pak choi and tempeh, then garnish with chilli, spring onions, and remaining black bean rayu.

title: Tahini Miso Udon Noodle Soup With Sweet & Smoky Chilli Glazed Aubergine, Pak Choi & Chives

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a saucepan and a large frying pan. Fill the saucepan with boiling water from the kettle, place it over high heat, and bring it back to the boil.
steps.label: Boil water in saucepan
steps.notes: Boil kettle first, then transfer water to saucepan on high heat to bring back to a boil.

steps.raw_text: Add the udon noodles to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes, or until tender but still al dente. Once cooked, drain and rinse the noodles under cold water. This removes excess starch and prevents them from becoming soggy. Set them aside in a colander to drain while you prepare the rest of the meal.
steps.label: Cook and rinse udon noodles
steps.notes: Cook for 5 minutes until tender but al dente. Rinse under cold water to remove excess starch.

steps.raw_text: Dice the aubergine into bite-sized pieces, about 2 cm cubes, and set aside. Halve or quarter the pak choi vertically. Place your large frying pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of neutral oil. Once the oil is hot, add the pak choi cut-side down and cook until it starts to char but still has a good bite, about 5-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then remove from the pan and keep warm. Wipe out the pan you used for the pak choi and add another drizzle of neutral oil. Return it to medium-high heat and add the aubergine cubes once the oil is hot. Cook for 8-10 minutes, until all sides are golden brown. When the aubergine is nearly ready, add half of the superseed chilli crunch , a drizzle of soy sauce if you have some (optional) and stir well to coat the pieces evenly.
steps.label: Prep and cook vegetables
steps.notes: Cook pak choi for 5-6 minutes. Cook aubergine for 8-10 minutes. Coat aubergine with half of the superseed chilli crunch and optional soy sauce at the end.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, rinse the saucepan you used for the noodles and place it back over medium heat. Add the shiitake ginger broth and warm it up gently. If you prefer a more brothy consistency, add a splash of water (about 50 ml), keeping in mind that the broth will be slightly diluted once added to the udon.
steps.label: Warm shiitake ginger broth
steps.notes: Rinse the noodle saucepan before reusing. Warm broth gently over medium heat. Optionally add 50 ml of water.

steps.raw_text: For the final step before serving, boil your kettle again. Set the colander of rinsed udon noodles over the sink and pour the boiling water over them to warm them through, then drain well. In the meantime, finely chop the chives and set them aside.
steps.label: Reheat noodles and chop chives
steps.notes: Boil kettle again and pour over noodles in colander to warm them. Finely chop chives in the meantime.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the udon noodles between serving bowls and ladle over the shiitake ginger broth . Top with the charred pak choi and the smoky, chilli glazed aubergine pieces. Finish by drizzling over the remaining superseed chilli crunch , and a sprinkle of the chopped chives . Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and serve soup
steps.notes: Divide noodles, ladle broth, top with pak choi, aubergine, remaining chilli crunch, and chopped chives.

title: Tandoori Tofu Naan Wraps With Cooling Mint Yoghurt, Pickled Red Cabbage & Fresh Spinach

steps.raw_text: Tender tofu bites are tossed in a tandoori marinade made with garlic, ginger, lemon and spices
steps.label: Marinate tofu
steps.notes: Toss the tofu bites in the tandoori marinade containing garlic, ginger, lemon, and spices.

steps.raw_text: roasted until charred
steps.label: Roast tofu
steps.notes: Roast the marinated tofu in the oven until it gets charred.

steps.raw_text: tangy pickled red cabbage
steps.label: Pickle red cabbage
steps.notes: Prepare the pickled red cabbage/onion using vinegar, sugar, and spices.

steps.raw_text: cool minted yoghurt
steps.label: Make minted yoghurt
steps.notes: Mix the mint and oat yoghurt to create the cooling minted yoghurt.

steps.raw_text: freshly baked, pillowy soft garlic and herb naan
steps.label: Bake naan
steps.notes: Bake the garlic and herb naan flatbread until soft and warm.

steps.raw_text: smothered in a cool minted yoghurt, tangy pickled red cabbage and fresh spinach. All wrapped in a freshly baked, pillowy soft garlic and herb naan.
steps.label: Assemble wraps
steps.notes: Assemble the wraps by placing the roasted tofu, minted yoghurt, pickled cabbage, and fresh spinach inside the baked naan.

title: High Protein Tempeh Sausage & Broccoli Lasagne In Rich Tomato Sauce With Creamy Miso Bechamel
High Protein Tempeh Sausage & Broccoli Pasta In Creamy Garlic Sauce With Toasted Walnut Pangrattato
Rich & Creamy Tempeh Tikka Masala With Toasted Flaked Almonds, Fresh Coriander & Basmati Rice

steps.raw_text: Meaty chunks of tempeh are marinated and cooked in a tikka spiced plant-based yoghurt
steps.label: Marinate tempeh in tikka spiced yoghurt
steps.notes: Combine the tempeh chunks with the tikka spiced plant-based yoghurt to marinate.

steps.raw_text: cooked in a tikka spiced plant-based yoghurt
steps.label: Cook marinated tempeh
steps.notes: Cook the marinated tempeh chunks in a pan until lightly browned.

steps.raw_text: basmati rice
steps.label: Cook basmati rice
steps.notes: Boil the basmati rice until fluffy.

steps.raw_text: then simmered in a rich and creamy masala sauce gently spiced with garlic, ginger, cumin and cardamom.
steps.label: Simmer tempeh in masala sauce
steps.notes: Add the masala sauce ingredients (garlic, ginger, cumin, cardamom, tomato, coconut milk) to the tempeh and simmer.

steps.raw_text: toasted flaked almonds
steps.label: Toast flaked almonds
steps.notes: Gently toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan until golden.

steps.raw_text: Served with toasted flaked almonds, fresh coriander and fluffy rice.
steps.label: Garnish and serve
steps.notes: Serve the tikka masala over fluffy rice, garnished with toasted almonds and fresh coriander.

title: Thai Green Curry With Mangetout, Crispy Tofu, Jasmine Rice, Chilli & Lime

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle and take out two saucepans and a frying pan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and gather two saucepans and a frying pan to prepare for cooking.

steps.raw_text: Place the jasmine rice in a small saucepan and cover with 2.5x its volume in water. Bring to the boil and once it's bubbling, reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 8-10 minutes or until tender but al dente.
steps.label: Cook jasmine rice
steps.notes: Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 8-10 minutes until tender but al dente.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Cut the tofu into 1.5cm cubes and fry for 5-8 minutes or until golden on all sides. Season with a dash of soy sauce or salt. Remove from the pan and then add the mangetout and fry them for 3 minutes or lightly charred but still with some crunch.
steps.label: Fry tofu and mangetout
steps.notes: Fry 1.5cm tofu cubes for 5-8 minutes until golden, then fry mangetout for 3 minutes until lightly charred but crunchy.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile empty the curry sauce into your other saucepan and warm through over a medium-low heat for 3-5 minutes.
steps.label: Warm the curry sauce
steps.notes: Warm the curry sauce over medium-low heat for 3-5 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Thinly slice the red chilli and quarter the lime for garnish and set aside.
steps.label: Prep chilli and lime garnish
steps.notes: Thinly slice the red chilli and quarter the lime, then set aside for serving.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the sauce between serving bowls, then add the tofu , mangetout and jasmine rice . Garnish with red chilli and a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish bowls
steps.notes: Divide sauce, tofu, mangetout, and rice into bowls. Garnish with sliced chilli and a squeeze of lime.

title: Brothy Thai Red Curry Bowl With Red Pepper, Pak Choi, Tofu, Charred Lime & Brown Rice

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle and take out two saucepans and a frying pan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set up two saucepans and one frying pan.

steps.raw_text: Place one of your saucepans over medium-high heat and fill it with boiling water from the kettle. Add the long grain brown rice , bring it back to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium. Simmer for 15–18 minutes, until the rice is tender but still al dente. Once ready, remove from the heat, drain any excess water, then return the rice to the pan. Cover with a lid to steam and keep warm.
steps.label: Cook the brown rice
steps.notes: Simmer the rice for 15–18 minutes until tender but al dente, then cover to steam.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, place your frying pan over medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Core the red pepper and trim the pak choi , then slice both into long strips. Add them to the hot pan and cook for 5–6 minutes, until lightly browned and tender but still with a bite. Remove from the pan and set aside.
steps.label: Prep and sauté vegetables
steps.notes: Sauté sliced red pepper and pak choi for 5–6 minutes until lightly browned but still crisp.

steps.raw_text: Cut the lime in half, then place the frying pan back over medium heat. Add the lime halves cut-side down and cook for 2–3 minutes, until charred.
steps.label: Char the lime halves
steps.notes: Cook cut-side down in the frying pan for 2–3 minutes until charred.

steps.raw_text: Wipe the frying pan clean and return it to medium heat with another drizzle of oil. Tear the tofu into bite-sized pieces with your hands and add to the pan. Cook for 5–6 minutes, until the edges are golden and crispy. Season with salt and pepper, or with a dash of soy sauce and pepper.
steps.label: Tear and fry tofu
steps.notes: Fry torn tofu pieces for 5–6 minutes until golden and crispy, then season.

steps.raw_text: Place the other saucepan over medium heat and add the thai red curry sauce . Warm through for 2–3 minutes, until piping hot. Add water to adjust the consistency. Keep it thick and creamy with just a splash of water, or add 100–150ml (double for 4 portions) to make it more brothy. Adjust the seasoning with a pinch of salt to taste. STEP 6 To serve, divide the long grain brown rice between serving bowls and pour over the thai red curry sauce . Top with the sautéed pak choi , red pepper , and crispy tofu . Finish with a squeeze of charred lime and a garnish of picked coriander leaves . Enjoy!
steps.label: Warm curry sauce and plate
steps.notes: Warm the curry sauce for 2–3 minutes, adjust consistency with water, and assemble the bowls.

title: Thai Red Curry Hispi Cabbage With Black Lentils, Lime Yoghurt, Toasted Peanuts, Fresh Coriander & Fluffy Rice

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out a saucepan and an ovenproof skillet. If you don’t have an ovenproof skillet, take out a frying pan and a baking tray instead.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare pans
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C or 200°C fan. Prepare alternative pans if you do not have an ovenproof skillet.

steps.raw_text: Place your skillet or frying pan over a high heat. Add the peanuts and dry-fry (without oil) until toasted. Set aside and wipe the pan clean with some kitchen towel.
steps.label: Dry-fry peanuts in skillet
steps.notes: Dry-fry without oil over high heat until toasted, then wipe the pan clean.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, cut the hispi cabbage into quarters lengthways. Rub with a generous amount of olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Using the same pan you toasted the peanuts in, add the hispi cabbage cut-side down and fry until charred. Flip and repeat on the other cut side. Once the cabbage is nicely charred, scatter over the drained and rinsed black lentils and pour in the coconut curry sauce . Turn off the heat, flip the cabbage quarters onto their backs so the cut sides face up, and transfer to the oven. Roast until tender in the centre and charred at the edges, about 15 minutes. Alternatively, if you are using a frying pan with a baking tray, transfer the charred hispi cabbage wedges and add the lentils and curry sauce and roast in the oven.
steps.label: Prep, char, and roast cabbage
steps.notes: Char cabbage on both cut sides before adding lentils and curry sauce. Roast in the oven for about 15 minutes until tender.

steps.raw_text: While the hispi cabbage is roasting in the oven, add the basmati rice to your saucepan and cover with twice its volume of water. Place over a medium-high heat and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid, and cook until fluffy, about 8 minutes.
steps.label: Boil and cook basmati rice
steps.notes: Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low heat for about 8 minutes until fluffy.

steps.raw_text: Pick the coriander leaves for garnish.
steps.label: Pick coriander leaves for garnish
steps.notes: Pick the leaves and set aside for final plating.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the hispi cabbage wedges and spoon over the thai red curry sauce . Drizzle with the coconut lime drizzle and finish by scattering over the coriander leaves and toasted peanuts . Serve with a bowl of fluffy basmati rice on the side. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate cabbage, rice, and toppings
steps.notes: Divide cabbage, spoon over curry sauce, drizzle with coconut lime, scatter coriander and peanuts, and serve with rice.

title: Thai Red Curry Sweet Potato Fritters Over Crunchy Mixed Veg & Quinoa Slaw With Aromatic Red Curry Dressing

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a saucepan and a large frying pan (non-stick works best for fritters).
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set up your cooking pans.

steps.raw_text: To prepare for the quinoa slaw, fill a saucepan with boiling water from the kettle and place it over medium-high heat. Once it’s bubbling, add the quinoa and cook for 6–8 minutes, or until al dente. Drain and set aside, keeping it warm. Finely slice the red and white cabbage wedges (using a mandolin if you have one), and place them in a bowl with a sprinkle of salt. Massage the cabbage to help it release its natural juices and soften. If you like, add a splash of vinegar and a drizzle of oil at this stage. Set aside until assembling the meal in Step 5.
steps.label: Cook quinoa and prep cabbage
steps.notes: Cook quinoa for 6-8 minutes until al dente. Slice and massage cabbage with salt.

steps.raw_text: Finely slice spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Grate the sweet potato into a large mixing bowl using the medium-size side of the grater. Add the fritter dry mix , the white part of the spring onions and season well with salt and pepper, and give it all a good mix until well combined and the texture is like a dough. Make your fritters using your hands, aiming for approximately 1cm thick and 10cm in diameter. They don't need to be perfect circles as rougher edges will turn nice and crispy! If the fritters don't stick together, you can add a splash of water to the mix as required. However the less moisture in the batter, the crispier the fritters will get when cooking and they will also bind together more as they're fried.
steps.label: Prep and shape sweet potato fritters
steps.notes: Grate sweet potato, mix with dry ingredients, and shape into 1cm thick, 10cm wide patties.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over a medium heat and add a neutral oil (e.g. rapeseed, sunflower, groundnut oil). The example image is shallow fried to make them extra crispy, but you can just add a drizzle of oil if you prefer less. Fry the fritters in batches for 4-5 minutes on each side or until crispy on the outside and cooked through in the centre. You should get around 2-3 fritters per person.
steps.label: Fry fritters until crispy
steps.notes: Fry in batches for 4-5 minutes on each side over medium heat until cooked through.

steps.raw_text: To finish off the quinoa slaw, combine the cooked quinoa , sliced & marinated cabbage slices, sesame seeds , spring onion greens with a splash of red Thai curry dressing . Season to taste with salt and pepper and reserve the remaining of the dressing to drizzle over the fritters. We recommend reserving some sesame seeds and spring onion for garnishing too.
steps.label: Assemble the quinoa slaw
steps.notes: Combine cooked quinoa, marinated cabbage, sesame seeds, spring onion greens, and dressing.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the salad between serving plates or bowls, top with the fritters and drizzle over the red Thai curry dressing . Garnish with any remaining sesame seeds and spring onions and enjoy!
steps.label: Plate, drizzle dressing, and garnish
steps.notes: Divide slaw, top with fritters, drizzle remaining dressing, and garnish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

title: Thai Red Curry With Noodles, Red Pepper, Chestnut Mushrooom, Courgette, Lime & Coriander

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle then take out a deep frying pan or wok.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pan
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set up your cooking vessel.

steps.raw_text: Place the vermicelli noodles into a heatproof bowl, pour boiling water over from your kettle to cover and leave the noodles to cook until tender, around 3-5 minutes. Drain and set aside to keep warm.
steps.label: Soak and drain vermicelli noodles
steps.notes: Leave noodles to cook in boiling water for 3-5 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.

steps.raw_text: Roughly chop the coriander leaves, cut the lime into quarters and set aside for garnish. Cut the chestnut mushrooms into quarters, deseed and slice the red pepper , and cut the courgette into bite-sized pieces - about 2 cm chunks.
steps.label: Chop vegetables and garnish herbs
steps.notes: Chop coriander and quarter limes for garnish. Cut mushrooms into quarters, slice peppers, and cut courgettes into 2 cm chunks.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan or wok over a medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the prepared chestnut mushrooms , red pepper and courgette and cook until tender but al dente, around 5-10 minutes. Pour in the red Thai curry sauce and cook until warmed through, around 2-3 minutes. Season to taste with salt or a splash of soy sauce.
steps.label: Stir-fry vegetables and warm curry
steps.notes: Cook vegetables over medium heat for 5-10 minutes until tender but al dente. Add curry sauce and warm through for 2-3 minutes. Season to taste.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, divide the vermicelli noodles between serving bowls and ladle over the red curry sauce with vegetables . Garnish with some freshly chopped coriander and a good squeeze of fresh lime juice. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble bowls and garnish curry
steps.notes: Divide noodles, ladle curry and vegetables, then garnish with coriander and fresh lime juice.

title: Fragrant Thai Tom Yum Noodle Soup With Tofu, Pak Choi, Button Mushrooms, Coriander & Lime

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out two saucepans and a frying pan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and prepare pans
steps.notes: Boil the kettle and set out two saucepans and one frying pan.

steps.raw_text: Place one of your saucepans over a medium heat and fill with the boiling water from the kettle. Add the flat rice noodles and cook for 5–6 minutes, or until tender but still al dente. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside in a colander to drain.
steps.label: Cook and drain rice noodles
steps.notes: Cook noodles for 5–6 minutes until tender but al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.raw_text: Cut any larger button mushrooms in half and leave any smaller ones whole. Place your frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil and fry the mushrooms until lightly browned, about 4–5 minutes. Season with salt or a dash of soy sauce, if you have some to hand.
steps.label: Prep and fry button mushrooms
steps.notes: Halve larger mushrooms and fry for 4–5 minutes until lightly browned. Season with salt or soy sauce if available.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, trim the base of the pak choi and slice it lengthways into long pieces. Dice the tofu into bite-sized cubes. Pick the coriander leaves from the stalks, cut the lime in half, and set aside for garnish.
steps.label: Prep pak choi, tofu, and garnish
steps.notes: Trim and slice pak choi, cube tofu, pick coriander leaves (keep stalks for broth), and halve the lime.

steps.raw_text: Place the second saucepan over a medium heat and add the tom yum broth , diced tofu , and 250ml water (double the quantity for 4 portions). Bring to a gentle simmer. For extra flavour, you can add the coriander stalks and the zest of the lime to the broth. Once the broth is bubbling, add the sliced pak choi and cook for a further 2–3 minutes, until tender but still with a little bite. Add the drained flat rice noodles to the broth and warm through for about 1 minute, then remove from the heat. If you added the coriander stalks, remove these before serving.
steps.label: Simmer broth with tofu and vegetables
steps.notes: Simmer broth with tofu (and optional coriander stalks/lime zest). Add pak choi for 2–3 minutes, then warm noodles for 1 minute. Remove coriander stalks before serving.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the tom yum noodles between serving bowls and top with the sautéed button mushrooms . Finish with a scattering of coriander leaves and a generous squeeze of fresh lime juice. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish noodle soup
steps.notes: Divide noodles and broth into bowls, top with fried mushrooms, coriander leaves, and fresh lime juice.

title: Black Bean Chilli Enchiladas Topped With Cashew Cheese Sauce & A Zingy Cherry Tomato Salsa

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan and take out an ovenproof dish or roasting tray sized to snugly fit the number of enchiladas (2 for a 2-person portion and double the size for a 4-person portion).
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare baking dish
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan). Prepare a snugly fitting ovenproof dish or roasting tray.

steps.raw_text: Drain the black beans and add them to a mixing bowl along with the enchilada sauce to make the enchilada filling mixture. Add a few tablespoonfuls of the mixture to the bottom of the ovenproof dish or roasting tray and spread evenly to create a shallow layer of sauce. Divide the remaining mixture between the flour tortillas , wrap them, and place them on top of the sauce. Pour the cashew cheese sauce all over the enchiladas. Bake in the oven for 15–20 minutes, or until the cheese sauce and tortillas have firmed up and turned golden. Check that the enchiladas are piping hot in the centre before serving.
steps.label: Assemble and bake the enchiladas
steps.notes: Bake for 15–20 minutes (midpoint 18 minutes used for bake time) until cheese sauce and tortillas are golden and firmed up, and the centre is piping hot.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, finely dice the red onion and cut the cherry tomatoes into quarters. Place them in a small bowl and toss with a little extra virgin olive oil, sea salt, and a squeeze of half a fresh lime to taste. This is your cherry tomato salsa. Pick the coriander leaves and roughly chop them for garnish.
steps.label: Prepare cherry tomato salsa and coriander
steps.notes: Can be prepared in the meantime while the oven preheats or while the enchiladas bake.

steps.raw_text: Once cooked, remove the enchiladas from the oven. Spoon over the cherry tomato salsa , scatter over the fresh coriander , and squeeze over the remaining lime juice . Divide between serving plates and enjoy!
steps.label: Garnish and serve the enchiladas
steps.notes: Spoon over salsa, scatter coriander, squeeze remaining lime juice, and plate.

title: Tofu Satay Skewer Bowl With Zingy Smacked Cucumbers, Pink Radish, Sushi Rice & Sesame Peanut Garnish

steps.raw_text: Take out a large frying pan, a small saucepan and a large bowl.
steps.label: Gather pans and large bowl
steps.notes: Gather the frying pan, saucepan, and large bowl before starting.

steps.raw_text: Place the sushi rice your small saucepan and pour over 2x its volume in water. Bring to the boil and once it's bubbling, reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and cook for 8-10 minutes until rice is tender and all water has been absorbed. Turn off the heat and let it steam.
steps.label: Cook and steam sushi rice
steps.notes: Cook covered for 8-10 minutes once bubbling, then turn off heat to steam.

steps.raw_text: Place the cucumber on a chopping board. Smash it gently along the length using a rolling pin or a heavy pestle until it splits, then chop diagonally into 1-2 inch diagonal slices. Place them into your bowl, sprinkle with salt, and toss to coat. Let them to sit for a while you prepare the rest of the meal.
steps.label: Smash and salt the cucumbers
steps.notes: Let the salted cucumbers sit while preparing the rest of the meal.

steps.raw_text: Cut or tear the tofu into bite-sized chunks. We recommend tearing or cutting the block in half, then in half again, and so on until you have around 16 pieces. Carefully thread the tofu pieces onto the skewers , aiming for about four large pieces per skewer.
steps.label: Cut and thread tofu skewers
steps.notes: Cut or tear tofu into about 16 pieces, aiming for 4 pieces per skewer.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add the tofu skewers and fry until all sides are golden. Drizzle a tablespoon of satay sauce over each skewer, turning to coat all the tofu pieces. Cook for another 1–2 minutes, until the sauce is caramelised and coats the tofu. Reserve the rest of the satay sauce.
steps.label: Fry and glaze tofu skewers
steps.notes: Fry until golden, then cook for 1-2 minutes with satay sauce until caramelized.

steps.raw_text: Roughly chop the radishes and set aside. When everything else is nearly ready, drain the excess liquid off the smacked cucumbers and then toss in the cucumber dressing . STEP 6 Divide the sushi rice between serving bowls and top with the satay tofu skewers . Drizzle over the remaining satay sauce , and serve with the smacked cucumber salad and radishes on the side. Finish with the peanut sesame garnish and enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish serving bowls
steps.notes: Drain cucumbers before dressing. Assemble bowls with rice, skewers, sauce, salad, radishes, and garnish.

title: Tofu Tikka Kebabs Over Spiced Rice With Mint Yoghurt, Juicy Cherry Tomatoes & Pink Onion Pickle

steps.raw_text: Preheat your oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Take out two baking trays and a saucepan.
steps.label: Preheat oven and prepare trays
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 200°C or 180°C fan. Prepare two baking trays and a saucepan.

steps.raw_text: Roughly tear the tofu into chunks with your hands. We recommend tearing the block in half, then in half again, and so on until you have around 16 pieces. Place them into a bowl with the tikka marinade and mix carefully to avoid breaking them apart.
steps.label: Tear and marinate tofu chunks
steps.notes: Tear tofu into roughly 16 pieces and mix gently with the tikka marinade to avoid breaking.

steps.raw_text: Place the basmati rice into your saucepan along with the rice spice mix , then cover with twice its volume of water. Place over a medium-high heat, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover with a lid. Leave to cook until light and fluffy, around 8 minutes.
steps.label: Cook spiced basmati rice
steps.notes: Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for around 8 minutes until light and fluffy.

steps.raw_text: Run the bamboo skewers under the tap (this will stop them from burning), then carefully thread the marinated tofu pieces onto the skewers, aiming for around four pieces per skewer. Place them on your baking tray and reserve any remaining marinade. Bake in the oven for 10 minutes, then turn them over, brush over the remaining marinade and bake for another 10 minutes until lightly charred at the edges.
steps.label: Skewer and bake tofu kebabs
steps.notes: Soak skewers first. Bake for 10 minutes, turn, brush with remaining marinade, and bake for another 10 minutes.

steps.raw_text: Trim the green beans and place them on another baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add them to the oven for the final 8 minutes of the tofu skewers’ cooking time.
steps.label: Prep and roast green beans
steps.notes: Trim beans, season, and roast in the oven during the final 8 minutes of the tofu's cooking time.

steps.raw_text: Meanwhile, quarter the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the mint leaves (reserving a few whole leaves for garnish). Stir the chopped mint through the organic soy yoghurt to make your mint yoghurt.
steps.label: Prepare tomatoes and mint yoghurt
steps.notes: Quarter tomatoes, chop mint (reserving some whole leaves), and stir into the soy yoghurt.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the spiced rice between serving bowls and top with the tofu tikka kebab skewers and roasted green beans . Add the cherry tomatoes and pickled red onion on the side. Drizzle over the mint yoghurt and garnish with the remaining mint leaves. Enjoy!
steps.label: Plate and garnish the kebabs
steps.notes: Assemble spiced rice, skewers, green beans, tomatoes, pickled onion, and drizzle with mint yoghurt.

title: Chargrilled Tofu Tikka Massala Naan Wrap With Coconut Yoghurt, Pickled Onion & Coriander

steps.raw_text: Take out a grill or griddle pan and a saucepan. If you don’t have a grill pan, any pan that can withstand high heat will work well. This will help the tofu pieces get nicely charred. Alternatively, you can follow the instructions to oven-bake the tofu instead.
steps.label: Prepare pans and equipment
steps.notes: Can use a griddle pan, any high-heat pan, or prepare to oven-bake instead.
