steps.raw_text: Place your saucepan over medium heat and add the tikka sauce . Heat gently until bubbling. Once piping hot, turn off the heat and cover to keep warm.
steps.label: Heat tikka sauce in saucepan
steps.notes: Heat gently over medium heat until bubbling, then cover to keep warm.

steps.raw_text: In the meantime, tear the tofu into bite-sized pieces using your hands and add it to a mixing bowl along with a generous drizzle of olive oil and the marinade dry mix . Toss until everything is evenly coated.
steps.label: Tear and marinate tofu
steps.notes: Tear tofu into bite-sized pieces and toss with olive oil and dry marinade mix.

steps.raw_text: Place your grill pan over medium-high to high heat to preheat. Once hot, add the flatbreads one by one and dry grill for 1 minute on each side until warmed through. Set aside and keep warm. Brush or spray the grill pan with oil, then add the marinaded tofu pieces in a single layer. Grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until char marks form and the tofu releases easily from the pan. Season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Alternatively, you can roast the marinated tofu in the oven at 220°C / 200°C fan for 20-25 minutes, until crispy and charred at the edges.
steps.label: Grill flatbreads and tofu
steps.notes: Dry grill flatbreads for 1 minute per side. Grill tofu for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred. Alternatively, roast in the oven at 220°C (200°C fan) for 20-25 minutes.

steps.raw_text: To serve, spread the tikka sauce over the flatbreads and top with the chargrilled tofu . Finish with dollops of coconut yoghurt , red wine vinegar pickled red onion , and a garnish of picked coriander leaves. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish wraps
steps.notes: Spread sauce on flatbreads, top with tofu, coconut yoghurt, pickled onion, and coriander.

title: Thai Noodle Salad with Broccolini, Spicy Cashews, Pickles, Coriander & Satay Sauce
Tuscan Panzanella Salad, With Creamy Vegan Mozzarella, Golden Ciabatta Croutons & Caper-Spiked Vinaigrette

steps.raw_text: golden ciabatta croutons
steps.label: Toast the ciabatta croutons
steps.notes: Toast the ciabatta until golden and crunchy.

steps.raw_text: chopped salad of juicy ripe tomatoes, ... plant-based mozzarella, fresh basil and butterbeans
steps.label: Chop tomatoes, red onion, basil, and mozzarella
steps.notes: Chop the fresh ingredients and drain the butterbeans.

steps.raw_text: tangy caper and garlic infused vinaigrette
steps.label: Prepare the caper and garlic vinaigrette
steps.notes: Whisk together the capers, garlic, balsamic vinegar, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, and maple syrup.

steps.raw_text: all tossed in a tangy caper and garlic infused vinaigrette
steps.label: Toss the salad with the vinaigrette
steps.notes: Combine the chopped vegetables, croutons, mozzarella, butterbeans, and basil, then toss with the prepared vinaigrette.

title: Umami Broth & Greens With Crispy Chilli Tempeh, Vermicelli & Chiu Chow Chilli Sauce
Sweet Chilli Noodle Salad With Crispy Tofu, Julienned Vegetables & Baby Gem
Vietnamese Rice Noodle Salad With Peanut Lemongrass Sauce, Pickled Carrot & Daikon, Edamame & Toasted Peanuts

steps.raw_text: Boil the kettle, then fill a saucepan with one cup of boiling water and place it over a medium heat. Blanch the edamame for 1–2 minutes, then drain and set aside. Return the same pan to a medium heat and refill it with boiling water. Once bubbling, add the flat rice noodles and cook for 4–5 minutes, until tender but still al dente. Test the noodles regularly to ensure they don’t overcook and become soggy. Rinse under cold water and drain well. Transfer the noodles to a mixing bowl, toss with a drizzle of neutral oil (sesame oil is recommended) and a dash of soy sauce, then set aside.
steps.label: Blanch edamame and cook rice noodles
steps.notes: Blanch edamame for 1–2 minutes. Cook noodles for 4–5 minutes until al dente. Rinse under cold water and toss with oil and soy sauce to prevent sticking.

steps.raw_text: Slice the baby cucumber in half lengthways, then thinly slice each half. Finely shred the red cabbage (use a mandoline slicer if you have one). Sprinkle a little salt over each of the vegetables and gently massage them to improve the texture. Roughly chop the coriander — and that’s all your vegetables ready!
steps.label: Prep and massage the vegetables
steps.notes: Thinly slice cucumber, finely shred cabbage (using a mandoline if available), salt and massage them to improve texture, and roughly chop coriander.

steps.raw_text: Toast the peanuts and sesame seeds mix by dry frying in a small frying pan until golden, then chop or roughly crush them.
steps.label: Toast and crush peanuts and sesame seeds
steps.notes: Dry fry the mix until golden, then chop or roughly crush.

steps.raw_text: To serve, divide the the cooked flat rice noodles between two serving bowls, and top with cucumber , red cabbage , edamame and pickled carrot and daikon . Pour over the peanut lemongrass sauc e and finish with the toasted & crushed peanuts and sesame seeds mix and fresh coriander leaves. Enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and garnish noodle salad
steps.notes: Divide noodles into bowls, top with cucumber, cabbage, edamame, pickled carrot, daikon, peanut lemongrass sauce, toasted nuts/seeds, and coriander.

title: Vive 3 x Protein Bar Bundle
Vive Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Protein Bar 50g

steps.raw_text: Carefully curated with the perfect blend of heavenly hazelnut butter, golden peanut butter and whole roasted golden hazelnuts
steps.label: Blend ingredients to form the bar base
steps.notes: Combine the hazelnut butter, peanut butter, roasted hazelnuts, and other base ingredients from the ingredient list.

steps.raw_text: this is the bar for you!
steps.label: Shape the mixture into bars
steps.notes: Form the blended protein mixture into individual bar shapes.

steps.raw_text: coated in a deliciously delicate layer of Belgian dark chocolate.
steps.label: Coat with Belgian dark chocolate
steps.notes: Apply a delicate layer of Belgian dark chocolate coating to the shaped bars.

Vive Dark Chocolate Salted Caramel Protein Bar 50g

steps.raw_text: A nut butter-based 'ganache-style' filling, made with roasted nuts, sweet dates and velvety cocoa butter
steps.label: Prepare the ganache-style filling
steps.notes: Combine the roasted peanuts, dates, cocoa butter, and protein ingredients to form the ganache-style filling base.

steps.notes: Coat the prepared protein filling with a delicate layer of Belgian dark chocolate.

title: Wholewheat Casarecce In A Sweet & Spicy Pumpkin & "Nduja" Sauce With Crispy Sage & Broccoli
Wholewheat Ditalini Puttanesca With Chickpeas, Courgettes, Red Pepper & Fresh Parsley
Winter Caesar Salad With Orzo, Butternut Squash, Tempeh 'Lardons', Cavolo Nero & Candied Almond Crunch
Winter Harvest Bowl With Roasted Sweet Potato, Candied Walnuts & Maple Tahini Dressing

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, pre-heat your oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, then take out a large roasting tray and a saucepan.
steps.label: Boil kettle and preheat oven
steps.notes: Preheat oven to 220°C (or 200°C fan).

steps.raw_text: Dice the sweet potato into 1.5cm cubes, place into your roasting tray, toss through a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes or until crispy on the outside and cooked through. Add the walnuts to the roasting tray for the final 2-3 minutes of cooking time. These have already been partly roasted in our kitchen so they only need a few minutes to warm through!
steps.label: Dice and roast sweet potato and walnuts
steps.notes: Roast sweet potato for 15-20 minutes. Add walnuts for the final 2-3 minutes to warm through.

steps.raw_text: Pour boiling water from your kettle into your saucepan and place over a medium-high heat. Bring to the boil and once bubbling, add the quinoa . Reduce the heat to low-medium and cook until tender but al dente, around 8 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.label: Boil and cook the quinoa
steps.notes: Cook quinoa for around 8 minutes until tender but al dente, then drain.

steps.raw_text: Remove any hardy stems from the cavolo nero , using your hands to strip the leaves away from the stalk. Roll the leaves up very tightly in your hands, then use a sharp knife to finely slice the leaves. Place into a large mixing bowl, add a pinch of salt and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil (optional), then massage the cavolo nero with your hands until it softens. NB: This is a raw cavolo nero recipe, but if you're not a raw cavolo nero lover, you could boil or steam the leaves for 10 minutes or roast them in the oven for 10 minutes tossed in oil, salt and pepper to make them crispy.
steps.label: Prep and massage the cavolo nero
steps.notes: Massage with salt and olive oil until soft. Alternatively, boil, steam, or roast for 10 minutes if raw is not preferred.

steps.raw_text: Cut the apple in half, remove the core, then thinly slice.
steps.label: Core and slice the apple
steps.notes: Thinly slice the apple after removing the core.

steps.raw_text: To serve up, toss the cavolo nero , sweet potato and quinoa in half of the tahini dressing , then top with the apple slices , candied walnuts and a scattering of pomegranate seeds . Drizzle over the remaining dressing and enjoy!
steps.label: Assemble and dress the harvest bowls
steps.notes: Toss greens, sweet potato, and quinoa with half the dressing, then top with apple, walnuts, pomegranate, and remaining dressing.

title: Yaki Udon Noodles With Aubergine, Savoy Cabbage, Carrot, Mushroom & Omega 3 Superseed Furikake

steps.raw_text: Boil your kettle, then take out a saucepan and a large frying pan or a wok. Fill your saucepan with boiling water from your kettle, place over a high heat and bring to the boil for the noodles.
steps.label: Boil water in saucepan
steps.notes: Boil kettle first, then transfer to saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat.

steps.raw_text: Add the udon noodles to the boiling water and cook for 5-6 minutes, or until tender but still al dente. Once cooked, drain and rinse the noodles under cold water. This helps remove excess starch and prevents them from becoming soggy. Set them aside in a colander to drain.
steps.label: Cook and drain udon noodles
steps.notes: Cook for 5-6 minutes until tender but al dente. Rinse under cold water to remove excess starch.

steps.raw_text: Dice aubergine lengthways into ~2cm cubed pieces. Slice or quarter the chestnut mushrooms and slice the savoy cabbage ~1cm thick. Use a peeler to create carrot ribbons and thinly slice the spring onions .
steps.label: Prep and chop vegetables
steps.notes: Dice aubergine to 2cm, slice cabbage 1cm thick, peel carrot ribbons, and thinly slice spring onions.

steps.raw_text: Place your frying pan or wok over high heat and add a generous drizzle of neutral oil, or sesame oil if you have it, as it works well with this dish. Add the aubergine once the oil is hot and fry until soft and lightly golden on both sides, around 6-8 minutes. Then add the savoy cabbage and chestnut mushrooms and cook for a further 4-5 minutes until soft. You can add a small splash of water to help the vegetables steam and soften. Add the carrot ribbons last, along with the yaki udon sauce , and combine everything well. Finally, add the cooked and drained udon noodles. Toss everything together and cook for another minute or so over high heat to warm through the noodles. Add a splash of water or an extra drizzle of oil if it feels dry, and allow the sauce to start caramelising on the vegetables and noodles. STEP 6 To serve, divide the yaki udon between serving bowls and finish with sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of furikake seasoning . Enjoy!
steps.label: Stir-fry vegetables, noodles, and serve
steps.notes: Fry aubergine for 6-8 minutes, cabbage and mushrooms for 4-5 minutes, then toss with noodles and sauce for 1 minute. Garnish with spring onions and furikake to serve.
